review-044.title: A restart resurrects implementers removed by an operator reset
review-044.detail: Sticky-target removal depends on changedCells, which exists only in memory. After an operator reset, a running daemon ignores the removed implementer correctly. Restarting initializes the Router with the restored base policy; RuntimePolicy then sets the identical policy, leaving changedCells empty. The persisted implementer is consequently appended and pinned ahead of the current cell again. A focused reproduction printed `before restart: claude/opus` and `after restart: codex/sol` for the same saved preference after resetting the cell to Claude.

review-044.title: A stale operator row in SQLite stops the daemon from starting, with no way to recover from the CLI
review-044.detail: The RuntimePolicy constructor re-validates every stored routing_cells row and the routing_prefer row against the current catalog, and throws on the first failure. Factory construction therefore fails. Unlike routing/policy.json, these rows aren't reviewed alongside catalog changes. When a model is retired, a provider is removed from config, or a transport changes, a row that was valid when written becomes fatal at the next start. `limitless routing reset` goes through the HTTP API, so the operator can't clear the row without editing the database by hand.
review-044.failure_scenario: The operator runs `limitless routing set implement.medium some/model`. A later release adds some/model to REMOVED_MODELS (or the operator removes that provider from config.toml). On restart, `new Factory()` throws 'implement.medium: ... retired', the daemon exits, and every CLI command fails.

review-044.title: Any routing edit cancels every queued or about-to-start invocation in every role
review-044.detail: policyRevision is a single global signal. Any setPolicy or setPreferProviders call aborts it, even for an unrelated role or cell. Every run waiting for a slot, or between invocation creation and the model call, then reroutes. Runs in the second case also get a 'cancelled' invocation row with 'routing changed before model call'. That adds noise to invocation history and stats, and the run can lose its place in the provider queue.
review-044.failure_scenario: The operator edits triage.small while an implement run is queued for a claude slot. The implement admission is aborted and requeued, and the run moves behind newer waiters.

review-044.title: Stale operator cell or prefer in SQLite makes the daemon fail at startup, with no CLI/API way to recover
review-044.detail: The RuntimePolicy constructor re-validates every stored routing_cells row through `this.groups(...)` (validatePolicy against the current catalog) and every stored prefer through `validatePrefer`, and throws on the first failure. The Factory constructor builds RuntimePolicy without a try/catch, so the daemon fails to start. The only remedies are `limitless routing reset` and `DELETE /api/routing/...`, and both need the running daemon. The operator would have to edit SQLite by hand. The catalog changes routinely: models get retired into REMOVED_MODELS, config.toml models or providers get removed, and parts 3/4 make it runtime-driven. A cell that was valid when set can therefore brick the next

review-044.title: Any routing edit aborts every waiting slot acquisition in every run, including unrelated roles
review-044.detail: `router.policyRevision` is a single global AbortController. It is aborted on every setPolicy, whatever cell changed, and on every setPreferProviders. Each run that is queued in tracker.acquire/acquireFirst is aborted and re-routed, and it loses its place in the provider queue. An edit to `triage.trivial` therefore reshuffles queued implement and review calls on the same providers, and they rejoin at the back of the queue.

review-044.title: An invalid persisted operator cell or prefer entry stops the daemon from starting, with no way to recover through the CLI or API
review-044.detail: The RuntimePolicy constructor revalidates every stored operator cell and the stored `prefer` list against today's catalog and throws on the first failure. Factory's constructor does not catch it, so the daemon fails to start. Things that commonly cause this: a code upgrade retires a model (it moves to REMOVED_MODELS), or the operator removes a provider or model from config.toml. Unlike `routing/policy.json`, the operator layer lives only in SQLite, and the only supported way to edit it (`limitless routing reset`) needs a running daemon. review-044.title: Any routing edit aborts every pending slot wait for every role and discards its queue position
review-044.detail: `router.policyRevision` is a single global AbortController, aborted by every `setPolicy` and `setPreferProviders` call. Each invocation that is waiting for admission, preflight or the pre-call window therefore aborts, releases its place, clears `busy` and calls `route()` again. This happens even when the edit touched an unrelated role or cell (e.g. chat.default). With a contended provider, every edit sends all waiting runs to the back of the FIFO queue. A newer waiter can then overtake older ones, and a waiter already admitted between routing and the model call has its invocation row marked 'cancelled'.

review-044.title: `eval policy` now diffs the proposed overlay against a 'current' policy that includes operator overrides
review-044.detail: `evalPolicy()` returns `policy: this.policy`, which now comes from `router.getPolicy()` and includes the SQLite operator layer. `limitless eval policy` prints `policyDiff(data.policy, overlayPolicy(DEFAULT_POLICY, proposed))`. Every live operator override therefore shows up as a change that `--write` would make, although writing policy.json has no effect on those cells while the overrides exist. This misleads review of the eval recommendation.
review-044.failure_scenario: The operator sets implement.small to codex/sol. Running `limitless eval policy` then prints '@@ implement.small @@ - [codex/sol] + [<eval chain>]' as though `--write` would restore the eval chain, when the operator override still takes precedence.

review-044.title: Resetting a cell with no override still writes a history entry and sends an SSE message
review-044.detail: `writeRouting(key, null, …)` always inserts a history row and `setCell` always publishes, even when no operator cell existed. Repeated resets of a cell without an override fill the append-only history with null→null entries.
review-044.failure_scenario: Running `DELETE /api/routing/cells/implement/small` twice records two entries with oldValue null and newValue null and sends two SSE `routing` messages.

review-044.title: An invalid persisted operator cell or prefer entry stops the daemon from starting, and there is no supported way to recover
review-044.detail: The `RuntimePolicy` constructor re-validates every stored cell and the stored prefer list against today's catalog, and throws if any is invalid, which aborts `Factory` construction. Operator cells live in SQLite, not in the reviewed repo. A deploy that retires a model (REMOVED_MODELS), or a config.toml edit that removes a provider or model, can therefore stop the daemon from starting. `limitless routing reset` cannot help because it goes through the daemon's HTTP API, so the operator has to edit SQLite by hand. The provider enable/disable precedent named in the request does not fail like this.
review-044.failure_scenario: An operator sets `implement.small` to `['claude/x']`. A later release moves `claude/x` into REMOVED_MODELS. The daemon then fails at startup with 'implement.small: ... unknown model ID', and `limitless routing reset implement.small` fails with 'Cannot reach the Limitless daemon'.

review-044.title: `Factory.policy` now includes operator overrides, so the `eval policy` diff is misleading
review-044.detail: `factory.policy` now returns the Router's effective policy, operator layer included. `evalReport` returns it as `policy`, and `src/cli/eval.ts:75` calls `policyDiff(data.policy, overlayPolicy(DEFAULT_POLICY, proposed))`, labelling the output 'current effective → proposed effective'. For any cell the operator overrides, the diff shows a change from the operator value to the eval value. In reality, writing policy.json would not change that cell's effective routing, because the operator layer still wins. It can also report a change when the overlay itself is unchanged.
review-044.failure_scenario: The operator sets `triage.default` to `['codex/sol']` and the evals overlay has `triage.default` as `['claude/opus']`. Running `limitless eval policy` prints '@@ triage.default @@ - ["codex/sol"] + ["claude/opus"]' even though nothing would change.

review-044.title: Resetting a cell with no operator override still writes a history row and publishes an SSE change
review-044.detail: `setCell(role, cell, null)` always calls `writeRouting`, even when no operator row exists. It records an (old null → new null) history entry, invalidates the routing revision (which aborts waiting admissions in every in-flight invoke), and publishes a `routing` message. `GET /api/routing` also returns the whole unbounded history on every call.
review-044.failure_scenario: Running `limitless routing reset implement.small` twice adds a second null→null history row and needlessly re-routes every run waiting for a slot.

review-046.title: In panel review mode, a single-entry review chain hits needs_human whenever a finding is raised
review-046.detail: With a review chain, the verifier call goes through `call(request, constraints, ...)` with verifierConstraints(), which still sets `excludeModels: avoidModels` (the finders' models, reason "raised a candidate it would verify"). In chain mode this hard exclusion is kept; only `verify`-role excludeModels are cleared in context.ts:480. If cfg.reviewMode is "panel" and the operator pins one review model, every finder routes to that model. The verifier then excludes it, the chain is empty, and the run stops at needs_human. The existing test only covers a two-entry chain.

On the environment retry, verifyAttempt(1, [firstModel]) passes the earlier verifier's model there, not the implementer's. A chain that reuses that model logs "verify used the implementer's vendor/checkpoint ... because this run pinned it", which misattributes the reason.

review-046.title: Pinned verify chain drops the environment-retry exclusion and logs a misleading warning
review-046.detail: For role verify in chain mode, `excludeModels` is cleared. But in engine.ts:1553 verify's `excludeModels` doesn't hold the implementer. It holds the previous verifier (`firstModel`), excluded so the environment-blocked retry runs on a different verifier. With a chain like verify=[A,B], the retry can run on A again instead of moving to B. When it does, the warning at line 632-373 says "verify used the implementer's vendor/checkpoint ... because this run pinned it", which is false: A is the earlier verifier, not the implementer.

review-046.title: Preserve already-tried verifier exclusions for pinned chains
review-046.detail: Clearing excludeModels for every pinned verify invocation also clears the exclusion supplied by verifyAttempt for an environment-blocked retry. That exclusion identifies the first verifier, not the implementer. Consequently, the retry selects the same first chain entry again instead of advancing to another candidate. This defeats the existing independent retry behavior and can exhaust the retry while a usable second entry remains.

review-046.title: Pinned verify chain clears excludeModels, so the environment-blocked retry reruns the same verifier
review-046.detail: For the verify role, `excludeModels` is not the implementer's checkpoint. It is the first verifier's model, passed by `verifyAttempt(1, [firstModel])` (engine.ts:1553) so the environment-blocked retry gets a different verifier. The change sets `excludeModels: undefined` whenever verify has a chain, so the retry picks the first chain entry again even when the chain lists a fallback. The warning check at context.ts:634 then treats that excluded model as an avoided implementer checkpoint and logs "verify used the implementer's vendor/checkpoint (...) because this run pinned it", which is wrong.

review-046.title: A pinned chain throws away a decision model's last-resort result
review-046.detail: `if (!target && lastResort && !chain)` stops pinned runs from using a last-resort result. That result comes from a model inside the chain (a triage decision model that declined with `lastResort: true`), so using it would not be a fallback outside the chain. As written, a pinned triage experiment on a decision model that declines with low ambiguity goes to needs_human, while the same model in policy would have finished triage.

review-046.title: In configured panel review mode, a one-entry review chain can deadlock on the verifier's hard exclusion
review-046.detail: Under a review chain the panel verifier still routes with `excludeModels` set to the models that raised candidates (`verifierConstraints`), and the chain path does not relax it for the review role. If the chain has one entry, the finder that raised candidates is the only candidate and is excluded, so the verifier has no target and the run goes to needs_human. Production defaults to single mode, so this only affects configured panel systems.

In panel mode, the panel verifier is a `review`-role call built by `verifierConstraints(avoidVendors, avoidModels, …)`, and its `excludeModels` lists every model that raised a candidate. Chain mode ignores finder `target` pins and `only`, so every finder routes to the head of the chain. The verifier then rules out that same checkpoint, and with a one-model chain nothing is left. invoke asks the question and throws NoCapacityError. The `skip` wrapper converts only Preempted, so the run goes to needs_human after the finders have already been paid for. The request says "the production reviewer follows the review chain", and `li

I edited the existing pipeline test 'a review chain replaces configured finder preferences…' to use ["alpha/m"]. review-046.title: A pinned verify chain drops the rule that the retry uses a different verifier, so the retry reruns the same model
review-046.detail: For verify, chain mode sets `excludeModels: undefined`. The only `excludeModels` verify ever gets is `[firstModel]` on the environment-blocked retry (`verifyAttempt(1, [firstModel])`, engine.ts:1553). That rule is there to get a second opinion from a different model, not to enforce vendor independence. Each invoke starts with a fresh `tried` and the chain order wins, so with verify=[A, B] the retry runs A again even though the operator listed B as a fallback. The warning check also counts `excludeModels` and logs "verify used the implementer's vendor/checkpoint", but that checkpoint is the first verifier's, not the implementer's.
review-046.failure_scenario: models {verify: ["A", "B"]}. The first verify returns only environment-blocked criteria, so verifyAttempt(1, ["A"]) runs. The router gets the chain without excludeModels, picks A again, and logs a warning that blames the implementer's checkpoint.

review-046.title: A pinned triage model's last-resort decline is discarded and the run goes to needs_human
review-046.detail: `if (!target && lastResort && !chain)` turns off the last-resort path in chain mode. A decision model returns `decline.lastResort` when its answers are "sound but unsure: usable as the last resort when no other model can answer". In a pinned chain no other model can answer, and using that answer does not leave the chain, so the strict-routing rule doesn't require dropping it. As written, an experiment that pins triage to a decision-capable model fails whenever the model is unsure, even though its answer is usable.
review-046.failure_scenario: models {triage: ["<decision model>"]}. The model declines with lastResort=true, the next route finds no untried candidates, and the run goes to needs_human instead of using its answer.

review-046.title: Chain mode ignores independence even as a tie-break between `|` alternatives
review-046.detail: With `c.chain` set, every candidate gets rank 0, so `a|b` alternatives are ordered only by provider preference and headroom. If a review chain is `claude/opus|codex/sol` and the implementer is openai, codex/sol can win on headroom and trigger the 'because this run pinned it' warning, even though the operator offered an independent alternative in the same group. The request says the chain wins over soft rules, not that soft rules stop breaking ties among alternatives the operator called interchangeable. The existing post-review log "Review done by the implementer's vendor (no other vendor available)" is also untrue in this case.
review-046.failure_scenario: Implementer is codex/sol (openai) and models.review = ["claude/opus|codex/sol"], with codex having more headroom. Review runs on codex/sol, logs the pinned-vendor warning and also logs 'no other vendor available'.

review-051.title: Far over the ≤20-line budget; parallel reimplementation of worktree trust logic
review-051.detail: The request asks for a single recordWorktree call on resume, or a migration step, within 20 source lines. The change adds a 71-line module that independently rediscovers the admin dir: it scans worktrees/*, runs `worktree list` against the cache, checks uid/nlink/recursive inspection and pointer comparisons. review-052.failure_scenario: A factory repository is configured as `Octocat/Hello-World`, while GitHub returns a timed-out job whose check_run_url uses `octocat/Hello-World`. The eligible job is never rerun or classified.

review-052.title: Compare repository URL components case-insensitively
review-052.detail: GitHub repository names are case-insensitive, but this exact comparison rejects valid job responses whose canonical repository casing differs from the configured slug. Classification repeatedly throws before recording or rerunning the failure. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-casing.ts". Output: {"reruns":0,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job"]}, followed by "Expected 1 rerun for canonical repository casing; received 0".
review-052.failure_scenario: The configured repository is o/r, and GitHub returns https://api.github.com/repos/O/R/check-runs/11 for a valid timed-out job.

review-052.title: Existing restart-repair test fails waiting for its pause callback
review-052.detail: This unchanged test fails both in the full check and independently. Command: bun test test/pipeline.test.ts -t 'verify-change: restart-repair'. Output: "error: expect(received).toBeDefined()", "Received: undefined" at line 4304; "0 pass", "1 fail". Its fixed polling window expires before the expected repair pause is observed.
review-052.failure_scenario: Running the restart-repair scenario in this checkout leaves resume undefined after 300 waits of 20 milliseconds.

review-052.title: Closed tracked PRs emit failures without classification
review-052.detail: The request says “Classify each `pr.ci_failed` on a factory PR.” Closed PRs remain tracked by githubTracked, and diffPr emits pr.ci_failed when their CI changes from success to failure. This OPEN-only guard leaves ciPending false, bypassing classification entirely. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-tqsoDY/claude-501/ci-review.ENsEJZ/closed-pr.mjs`. Output: `{"feed":["pr.ci_failed"],"calls":["graphql"],"ciPending":false,"logs":[]}`, followed by `AssertionError: each emitted pr.ci_failed must enter REST classification`.
review-052.failure_scenario: A factory PR is closed while CI is still completing. Its saved closed snapshot has successful CI, then a timed-out check changes the rollup to FAILURE. The next poll emits pr.ci_failed but fetches no failure details and produces no classification. The saved snapshot prevents unchanged observations,

review-052.title: Isolate CI inspection errors to the affected PR
review-052.detail: Exceptions from classifyCi escape record and abort the repository's observation loop before later PRs are processed. Persistent missing CI details therefore starve unrelated PR observations. The same isolated check command above produced repeated 'GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/check-runs?filter=latest&per_page=100&page=1 (404)' and 'later PR saved state: null'; the assertion failed with 'Received: null'.
review-052.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR's CI-detail endpoint repeatedly returns 404 or malformed data. Every poll aborts there, so later PRs in the same repository never update their saved CI, review, closed, or merged state.

review-052.title: Deduplicate main-red alerts at repository scope
review-052.detail: The request requires: "Main is red on the same check: pause per-PR reactions for that check, and emit one ci.main_red item for the repository." Both emission paths use a key containing the check name, so different failing checks bypass repository deduplication. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-entry-review.test.ts". The two-check probe failed with Expected length: 1; Received length: 2.
review-052.failure_scenario: Both test and build fail on main and on a factory PR. One inspection emits two ci.main_red feed items for the same repository incident.

review-052.title: One PR's classifier error stops every later PR in the same repository from being polled
review-052.detail:
`classifyCi` reports problems by throwing: `Incomplete CI inspection`, `Ambiguous originating CI job`, `Incomplete failing check`, zod parse errors, and others. `record` does not catch them, so the error escapes `observe` and the per-repo catch in `tick` swallows it. `observe` calls `record` serially for each PR in the batch, so every PR after the failing one goes unrecorded that cycle. Nothing records its merge or close, its CI or review changes, or its access state.

Because `save()` writes `ciPending: true` before the classifier runs, the next poll retries the same inspection. When the cause is persistent, the repository's later PRs are starved indefinitely. Persistent causes include:
- j
review-052.failure_scenario: Repository has PRs A and B, in that order in the batch. A's failing job logs return 410, or A's workflow has two jobs with the same name and one times out. B is merged. Every poll throws while inspecting A, so B's `pr.merged` and its run-merge reconciliation never happen.

review-052.title: Feed excerpt is the start of the job log, not the failure
review-052.detail: `emit` is called with `log || f.line` and stores `quote(excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000))`. That is the first 2000 characters of the whole Actions job log. Actions logs begin with runner, OS and image preamble, plus checkout and setup groups, so the excerpt in `ci.needs_fix` almost never contains the failure. That makes it useless to whoever investigates the item.
review-052.failure_scenario: Any `ci.needs_fix` from an Actions job whose log is longer than about 2000 characters: the excerpt shows 'Current runner version ... Runner Image ...' rather than the failing assertion.

review-052.title: New `[github] ci_reruns` switch is not documented
review-052.detail: The GUIDE config table documents every `[github]` key (`poll`, `poll_seconds`), but the new `ci_reruns` switch is missing. It defaults to on and triggers paid CI reruns, so operators need to know it exists.
review-052.failure_scenario: An operator who wants to stop automatic reruns has no documented way to find the switch.

review-052.title: A table introduced by this change is split across two migrations; change is about twice the budget
review-052.detail: `ci_failures` is created in `20261005T0737-ci-failures.sql`, and this same change then adds `rerun_job` in a second migration. Neither has shipped, so the column belongs in the CREATE TABLE. The change is also about 500 source lines against a requested budget of about 250. The classifier is dense, with many inline guard-and-throw paths, which makes it hard to review and maintain.
review-052.failure_scenario: No runtime failure; this adds schema churn and maintenance cost.

review-052.title: A classifyCi exception aborts observation of every later PR in the repository, indefinitely
review-052.detail: record() awaits classifyCi with no error handling. classifyCi throws in many places (Incomplete failing check, Incomplete CI log, Ambiguous originating CI job, Outdated CI check completion, any non-200 REST read). The throw propagates out of observe(), whose loop `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries()) await record(...)` stops, so PRs after the failing one are never recorded. ciPending was already saved as true, so the same PR throws again every cycle. Merges, closes, review and comment items for the other PRs are lost, setGithubAccess(repo, null) never runs, and delivered runs waiting on a merge stay stuck. Before this change, record() could not fail on REST data.
review-052.failure_scenario: Reproduced in a copy of the repo with dependencies installed. PR 1 has rollup FAILURE but the REST check-run for 'test' shows success, and PR 2 is set to MERGED. After 10 poll cycles, PR 2's saved data is still undefined, and the logs repeat 'GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing chec

review-052.title: The failure signature uses the first line containing 'fail' or 'error', often an echoed action input
review-052.detail: ciSignature uses `lines.find(l => /timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i.test(l))`. GitHub Actions logs print each step's inputs (for example `fail-on-cache-miss: false` for actions/cache) long before the real failure. That line becomes the signature 'line' for every failure of the check. Ledger rows then record a meaningless 'failing test or error line'. Different failures at the same SHA share a signature, which breaks the 'one rerun per PR, SHA and signature' identity, and flakes cannot be told apart by test.
review-052.failure_scenario: In my scratch test, ciSignature('test', log, 'failure') returned 'fail-on-cache-miss: false' for a log whose real failure lines were '##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.' and 'AssertionError: expected 1 to be 2'.

review-052.title: A rerun is requested while the workflow run is still in progress, which uses up the only rerun and can raise an access problem
review-052.detail: Classification starts as soon as the rollup turns FAILURE, which happens while sibling jobs are still running. The code claims the rerun (claimCiRerun) and POSTs actions/jobs/{id}/rerun without checking that the run is completed. GitHub refuses to rerun jobs of a run that is still in progress (403). The claim is already spent, so the next pass sees the prior row as rerun_requested and emits ci.needs_fix, and the transient failure never gets its rerun. The 403 also goes through call() and ciCall, which treat it as an access problem: the repository is blocked with backoff and a 'forbidden' github.access_problem item is emitted.
review-052.failure_scenario: In a workflow with jobs 'smoke' and 'test', 'smoke' times out at minute 5 while 'test' runs until minute 15. The poller sees FAILURE and POSTs the rerun for 'smoke', and GitHub returns 403 because the run is in progress. The row stays rerun_requested, and the next poll emits ci.needs_fix without a r

review-052.title: Fail-fast matrix cancellations count as transient, so a pass on rerun is logged as false flake evidence
review-052.detail: Any 'cancelled' conclusion at the current head counts as transient. In a matrix with fail-fast (the default), one leg failing cancels the others. Each cancelled leg is rerun, usually passes, and gets outcome failed_then_passed. The request says a rerun that passes at the same SHA is the only evidence of nondeterminism that counts, so the ledger records nondeterminism that never happened. It also spends paid CI on reruns that were never needed.
review-052.failure_scenario: In a matrix test with legs [ubuntu, macos] and fail-fast: true, the ubuntu leg fails an assertion and the macos leg is cancelled. The macos leg is rerun, passes, and the ledger row shows outcome 'failed_then_passed' for macos.

review-052.title: The main-red state resets while main's newest commit is still running checks, which creates duplicate ci.main_red items
review-052.detail: A check counts as red only if the latest run on main's current HEAD is completed with a failure. When another commit lands on main while the check is still broken, its runs are in_progress, so red becomes false. Per-PR suppression lifts during that window, so the PR can be rerun or get ci.needs_fix. When main finishes red again, `episode` goes up and a new ci.main_red item is emitted. The request asks for one ci.main_red item per repository while main is red.
review-052.failure_scenario: Main is red on 'test' (episode 1). A PR lands on main, and while the new HEAD's 'test' is in progress a factory PR fails 'test' and gets rerun or reported as needs_fix. Main finishes red, and a second ci.main_red item (episode 2) is emitted.

review-052.title: The feed excerpt is the first 2000 characters of the job log, not the failure
review-052.detail: emit() stores `quote(excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000))`, where excerpt is the full job log. Actions logs start with runner, image and checkout setup output, so the excerpt rarely includes the failing test or error. That makes ci.needs_fix much less useful to whoever reads the feed.
review-052.failure_scenario: For a typical 50 KB Actions log the ci.needs_fix excerpt contains only 'Current runner version', 'Operating System', 'Runner Image' and checkout lines.

review-052.title: Observations the head epoch refuses are now dropped entirely, an unrequested behavior change
review-052.detail: Previously record() ignored observePrHead's result and still saved the snapshot (state, merge, feed items); only the head write was refused. Now a refusal returns early. While a round's push mark exists (including one left by a crashed run until it becomes terminal), the PR's merges, closes and comments are not observed.
review-052.failure_scenario: A round run crashes between beginPrPush and endPrPush and stays non-terminal. The PR is merged meanwhile, but the poller does not record the merge until the run is marked terminal.

review-052.title: A second migration adds a column to a table this same change creates
review-052.detail: Neither migration has shipped, so `rerun_job` belongs in the CREATE TABLE in 20261005T0737-ci-failures.sql. A separate ALTER adds churn.
review-052.failure_scenario: There is no runtime failure; this only adds an extra migration file and an extra ALTER at every fresh install.

review-053.title: A CI inspection error prevents later PRs from being observed
review-053.detail: Classifier errors propagate through record() and abort the repository's observation loop. A persistent error on the first PR therefore prevents subsequent PR snapshots and feed events from being saved, even though GraphQL returned them successfully. Command: `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. The unavailable-log fixture produced `later PR: {"saved":null,...}` and failed with `expect(received).not.toBeNull(); Received: null` after two polling cycles.
review-053.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has a failed Actions job whose logs endpoint repeatedly returns 404. A second PR in the same repository remains unobserved on every polling cycle.

review-053.title: Case-sensitive repository URLs reject valid GitHub jobs
review-053.detail: Repository resolution preserves user-supplied slug casing, while GitHub returns canonical casing in check_run_url. This exact string comparison rejects a valid job; rerun reconciliation has the same problem at line 258. Command: `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. With stored slug o/r and canonical URLs O/R, the fixture reported `{"reruns":0,"errors":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete failing job"]}` and failed with `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
review-053.failure_scenario: A repository is registered as mattflower/limitless, but GitHub returns check URLs containing MattFlower/limitless. Transient failures cannot rerun or finish classification.

review-053.title: Main-red failures never enter the flake ledger
review-053.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching failure evidence or recording a CiFailure. Consequently, non-security failures suppressed because main is red have no ledger signature, SHA, runner image, or outcome, contrary to the requirement to record each failure signature. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kw8EdQ/claude-501/ci-review-main-red.ts. Output on every poll: {"done":false,"posts":0,"ledgerRows":0,"mainRed":true}.
review-053.failure_scenario: Both the factory PR and main fail the test check. The classifier emits ci.main_red, but the failure is never recorded if the PR closes or receives another SHA before main recovers.

review-053.title: One CI inspection error starves later PR observations
review-053.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's observation loop. A persistent error for the first PR therefore prevents every later PR from saving even its successful GraphQL observation. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: "Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)" on consecutive polls and "second PR persisted: null"; assertion output: "expect(received).not.toBeNull() / Received: null".
review-053.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has deleted or unavailable Actions logs returning HTTP 404. A second PR in the same repository reports successful or merged state, but its observation is skipped on every poll until the first PR's inspection succeeds.

review-053.title: A later sibling-only attempt hides the originating rerun
review-053.detail: Reconciliation searches only the workflow's latest attempt. Selective job reruns can create a later attempt containing another job, so the originating job's completed rerun exists only in an earlier attempt. The classifier then throws on every inspection rather than recording its result. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". The fixture supplied a successful originating job in attempt 2 and another job in attempt 3; output was "error: Ambiguous CI rerun job".
review-053.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2, where it succeeds. Before the next poll, someone reruns sibling job B, creating attempt 3 containing only B. Job A remains rerunning indefinitely despite available successful evidence at the same SHA.

review-053.title: Completed skipped or neutral reruns never resolve
review-053.detail: Reconciliation handles success and conclusions in bad, then continues for all other conclusions—even completed jobs. A skipped or neutral rerun remains rerunning permanently, and a SUCCESS rollup repeatedly returns false. Direct check `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `Skipped rerun: {"done":false,"outcome":"rerunning","feed":0}` and `ASSERTION FAILURE: completed skipped rerun must resolve pending inspection` (`false !== true`).
review-053.failure_scenario: A failed job is rerun, but its job condition excludes subsequent attempts, so attempt 2 completes as skipped and the rollup becomes SUCCESS. The original ledger row remains rerunning and REST inspection continues indefinitely across restarts.

review-053.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
review-053.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's entire observation loop. Later PRs are skipped even though their GraphQL snapshots were fetched successfully. The same ordering repeats on subsequent polls, so a persistent CI-detail error can indefinitely suppress merge, close, review, and CI observations for other PRs. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-o0sYkW/claude-501/ci-review-poller.ts`. Output: `{"firstPrSaves":2,"secondPrSaves":0,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/main (500)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: commits/main (500)"]}`.
review-053.failure_scenario: Two PRs are tracked in one repository. The first has failed CI and its CI REST inspection returns HTTP 500; the second has a valid passing or merged snapshot. Every poll aborts on the first PR before saving the second.

review-053.title: Inspect main's commit statuses independently of the PR's context types
review-053.detail: The shared checks helper fetches legacy commit statuses only when the PR snapshot contains status contexts or is truncated. Main can publish a failing legacy status with the same name as the PR's Actions check, so this condition hides main's failure and incorrectly permits a rerun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` against that fixture produced `main-status {"outcomes":["rerunning"],"feed":[],"reruns":1,"mainStatusesRequested":false}`.
review-053.failure_scenario: Main has a failing legacy commit status named test, while the factory PR has a timed-out Actions check named test and no legacy status contexts. The classifier reruns the PR job and emits no ci.main_red item.

review-053.title: One CI inspection error starves other PRs in the repository
review-053.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record() and abort the repository's entire observation loop. The failing PR retains ciPending and is retried first every cycle, preventing later PRs from recording CI, reviews, or merge state. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pKEV2z/claude-501/review-poller.ts`. After three cycles, output was `"savedPrs": [1,1,1], "secondPrObserved": false`, with `Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)` logged each cycle.
review-053.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has deleted or unavailable job logs returning 404; a second PR in the same repository has a valid observation.

review-053.title: Job reruns can also rerun downstream security tests
review-053.detail: GitHub's job rerun endpoint reruns the selected job and its dependent jobs. The security checks inspect only the selected job; the sibling lookup also filters immediately to that job's name. Consequently, a permitted transient rerun can automatically rerun a downstream security job, violating the security-test exclusion.
review-053.failure_scenario: A timed-out unit-test job has a dependent security-test job using `needs` and `if: always()`. Rerunning the unit-test job also reruns the security job.

review-053.title: Recognize test timeout diagnostics beyond Bun and Playwright
review-053.detail: The anchored timeout expression excludes legitimate test-owned timeout messages such as Node's `test timed out after 100ms`. These failures are classified as needing a fix instead of receiving the requested transient retry. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-pKEV2z/claude-501/review-ci.ts`. Output: `Node test timeout result: {"posts":0,"outcome":"failed","needsFix":1}`.
review-053.failure_scenario: An Actions job concludes failure and its log contains the Node test-runner diagnostic `test timed out after 100ms`.

review-053.title: Resolve definitively rejected reruns instead of waiting forever
review-053.detail: The rerun is claimed before the POST, but every non-201 response throws without resolving that claim. If GitHub explicitly rejects the request, subsequent inspections see run_attempt unchanged and retain rerun_requested indefinitely, emitting no ci.needs_fix. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: after explicit HTTP 403: {"outcomes":["rerun_requested"],"feed":[]}; assertion Expected: true, Received: false.
review-053.failure_scenario: A timed-out job is eligible for retry, but the token lacks Actions write permission and the rerun POST returns HTTP 403. GitHub never starts another attempt, leaving classification pending permanently.

review-053.title: Record main-red failures before suppressing PR reactions
review-053.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching the job evidence or recording the failure. Consequently, these failures never enter the ledger, despite the requirement to record each failure signature, SHA, runner image, and outcome. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: main-red inspection: {"ledgerRows":0,...}; assertion Expected: 1, Received: 0.
review-053.failure_scenario: A factory PR has a failed test check and main has the same failing check. Classification emits ci.main_red but creates no ci_failures row for the PR SHA.

review-053.title: A classification error in one PR stops observation of every later PR in the same repository
review-053.detail: `record` awaits `classifyCi` without catching its errors. `classifyCi` throws in many deliberately 'retryable' situations: any non-200 REST read (logs 404/410, access errors), zod parse failures, and the various 'Incomplete …' or 'Ambiguous …' checks. The error propagates out of the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in `observe`, so the PRs after this one are never recorded in that cycle. Because `ciPending` was already saved as true, the same PR throws again on every poll. A persistent condition such as expired job logs (410) therefore stops merge, close, CI and review detection for every later PR in that repository indefinitely. That in turn stalls reconcileMergedRuns and the l

Setup: PR #1 has a timed-out Actions job whose logs endpoint returns 410, and PR #2 in the same repository is then merged. After 10 polls (`bun test test/zz-review.test.ts -t starves`) there are 0 `pr.merged` items, where 1 was expected.

review-053.title: The feed excerpt is the first 2000 characters of the raw job log, which is usually runner setup boilerplate
review-053.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` quotes `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)`. GitHub Actions logs begin with runner, image and checkout setup output, so for real failures the excerpt rarely contains the failing line. The signature line is extracted separately, but the excerpt adds little diagnostic value.
review-053.failure_scenario: A typical Actions log with several KB of setup output before the failing test: the ci.needs_fix excerpt shows only the setup lines.

review-053.detail: The request asked for about 250 changed source lines. The classifier alone is 399 lines, plus about 80 in the poller, two migrations (the second only alters a table the first created in the same change), and store helpers. Much of the size comes from defensive cross-validation (completion timestamps, sibling ambiguity, annotation counts), which also creates many of the throw paths behind the blocker above.

The exception travels out of the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in `observe`, so every later PR in that GraphQL batch is never recorded that cycle. Their feed items (merged, ci_passed, conflicts) and their head bookkeeping are lost. `ciPending` is persisted as true before classification, so a persistent condition repeats the throw every cycle. One examples is a job whose logs have exp

A has a failing Actions job, and the logs endpoint returns 404 or 410 for it (logs not yet available, or expired). read() throws, observe() aborts, and B's newly merged state is never recorded. review-053.detail: The signature line is the first log line that matches `\b(error|fail(ed|ure)?)\b`. Setup noise can match first. review-053.detail: The request budgeted about 250 changed source lines. The classifier alone is about 400 lines, plus about 80 in the poller. review-053.detail: Reconciliation searches only the workflow's latest attempt. review-053.detail: bun test test/pipeline.test.ts --test-name-pattern 'verify-change: restart-repair' fails on both HEAD and the base commit with "expect(received).toBeDefined() / Received: undefined". The fixed readiness wait expires before the fixture reaches its repair-review checkpoint. This failure predates the change.
review-053.failure_scenario: Run the restart-repair test in this environment; resume remains undefined after the 300 iterations of the 20 ms wait.

review-053.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
review-053.detail: A classifyCi exception propagates through record() and aborts the repository's observation loop before later PR snapshots are saved. A persistently unavailable log therefore starves unrelated PRs on every poll. Probe: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probe.test.ts"`. With the first PR's log endpoint returning HTTP 404 and a second PR passing CI, repeated polls printed `NEXT_PR {"data":null,"errors":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)"]}`. The assertion requiring the second PR's snapshot failed with `Received: null`.
review-053.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR has an unavailable or expired job log. Later PRs in the same repository stop receiving persisted CI, review, and merge observations until that endpoint recovers.

review-053.title: Isolate CI inspection failures from other PR observations
review-053.detail: A classifier exception escapes record() and aborts observation of every subsequent PR in the repository. Repeated failures therefore prevent unrelated merges and closures from being recorded. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-review-repro.ts"` with the first PR's logs returning 500 produced `"secondPrSnapshot":null,"graphQLCalls":2` despite the second PR being merged.
review-053.failure_scenario: Two tracked PRs share a repository. The first has failing CI with an unavailable log endpoint; the second merges. Every poll aborts before recording the second PR.

review-053.title: Compare repository URL components without case sensitivity
review-053.detail: GitHub repository names are case insensitive, but check_run_url is compared against the configured slug verbatim. Canonical API URL casing can therefore reject a valid job. The rerun-resolution prefix check has the same problem. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-ci-review-repro.ts"` with configured o/r and returned O/R produced `"ledger":[],"needsFix":0,"rerunPosts":0,"pending":true` and repeated `Incomplete failing job` errors.
review-053.failure_scenario: A repository is configured with different capitalization from GitHub's canonical check_run_url. Every CI inspection fails before classification or rerunning.

review-053.title: Existing restart-repair test fails on both base and HEAD
review-053.detail: `bun test test/pipeline.test.ts -t 'verify-change: restart-repair'` exits 1 with `expect(received).toBeDefined()`, `Received: undefined`, and `0 pass / 1 fail`. The same command against a temporary snapshot of the base commit fails identically, so this is not introduced by this change.
review-053.failure_scenario: Run the isolated restart-repair test; its expected resume callback remains undefined when the wait expires.

review-053.title: Exclude security steps regardless of their conclusion
review-053.detail: The request states: “The ledger never quarantines a test, and never touches security tests.” This guard examines step names only when their conclusions are failures. A generic job containing successful security tests and a subsequent timed-out smoke test therefore passes the guard, enters the ledger, and receives a whole-job rerun, executing those security tests again. Reproduction command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-M50TQh/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-M50TQh/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-M50TQh/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-M50TQh/claude-501/security-step-review.mjs`. Output: `AssertionError: Jobs containing security tests must not be rerun`, with actual `["repos/o/r/actions/jobs/21/rerun
review-053.failure_scenario: A job named `test` runs a `security tests` step successfully, then times out during `smoke`. With reruns enabled and main green, the classifier records and reruns the entire job.

review-053.title: Exclude jobs containing successful security steps from reruns
review-053.detail: Security step names are checked only when the step failed. Rerunning an Actions job repeats its successful steps too, so a mixed job containing successful security tests and a later timeout passes this guard and reruns the security tests. A direct classifier probe with a successful step named "Security tests" produced reruns=1 and outcome="rerunning", contrary to the requirement to never touch security tests.
review-053.failure_scenario: A generic test job successfully runs a Security tests step, then another step times out. Its logs and annotations contain no security keywords, so the classifier reruns the whole job.

review-053.title: Persisted CI pauses bypass the GraphQL-change guard
review-053.detail: The request says: "Fetch the failing check runs and jobs by REST, only when the GraphQL state changed." A main-red inspection returns false and persists ciPending=true. This condition then calls classifyCi on every unchanged GraphQL observation, fetching default-branch and PR check runs again. Restoring the saved snapshot after restart takes the same unguarded path. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-j02dtj/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-j02dtj/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-j02dtj/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-j02dtj/claude-501/ci-main-red-review.ts. Output: "REST calls after initial GraphQL failure: 3", "REST calls after identical GraphQL poll: 6", "REST calls after restart with identical s
review-053.failure_scenario: A factory PR and main both fail the test check. After initial classification, the PR's GraphQL snapshot remains identical. Every subsequent poll, and the first poll after restart, repeats REST check-run inspection despite no GraphQL state change.

review-053.title: Main-red pause re-runs the REST inspection every poll cycle for every affected PR
review-053.detail: When a PR check matches a red main check, `paused` is set and classifyCi returns false. The poller then keeps `ciPending` true (`same && prev?.ciPending`), so each later poll repeats the inspection even though GraphQL has not changed. Each repeat fetches commits/main, the main check-runs and the PR check-runs, plus status pages and more pages on real repos. That breaks the requirement to fetch REST only when the GraphQL state changed. Main is fetched separately for each PR instead of once per repo. Delivered PRs poll every 15s, so each one costs about 720+ REST calls an hour while main is red. A handful of such PRs can use up the 5000/h token budget the rest of the factory shares, and main-r
review-053.failure_scenario: Ad-hoc test (test/review2.test.ts): 3 failing PRs, main check 'test' failing, GraphQL unchanged. Over 4 × 45s cycles the fake records 36 REST calls (commits/main, main check-runs and PR check-runs for each PR on every cycle).

review-053.title: Failure signature includes volatile text such as test durations, so the same flake gets a different signature on each run
review-053.detail: `ciSignature` takes the first log line matching error or fail verbatim (only the timestamp is stripped). For Bun that line is '(fail) slow [5000.01ms]', which includes the measured duration. The same test failing on another run or SHA gets a different signature, so the ledger cannot link occurrences of one flaky test by its 'failing test or error line'. Taking the first line that mentions 'error' anywhere in a full log can also pick setup noise instead of the real failure.
review-053.failure_scenario: The same test times out on two SHAs, logged as '(fail) slow [5000.01ms]' and '(fail) slow [5000.37ms]'. The ledger stores two unrelated signatures.

review-053.title: A second migration alters a table created in the same change
review-053.detail: 20261005T0737-ci-failures.sql creates ci_failures, and 20261005T084754-ci-rerun-job.sql immediately adds rerun_job. Neither has shipped, so the split is churn. The second file also uses a different timestamp format (with seconds) from its neighbours.
review-053.failure_scenario: No runtime failure; the schema history carries an extra step.

review-053.title: Change is roughly twice the requested budget and hard to review
review-053.detail: The request budgets about 250 changed source lines. The diff adds about 550 source lines: a 399-line classifier with deeply nested defensive checks, and extra poller state (ciKey, passing, completed, statusNames, ciPending). It also changes the poller so that a refused `observePrHead` now drops the whole observation, which is unrelated to CI classification. The density makes the defects above, such as the over-broad unsafe check, easy to miss.
review-053.failure_scenario: No runtime failure; maintainability and scope.

review-053.title: A throwing CI classification aborts observation of every later PR in the repository batch, every cycle
review-053.detail: classifyCi throws on many conditions: non-200 REST reads, zod parse failures, and 'Incomplete …' guards. record() awaits it without a catch, so the exception leaves observe()'s loop over `known` and is only caught by tick's `.catch`. The remaining PRs in that GraphQL batch are never recorded: no state save, no merged/closed/review feed items. The failing PR keeps ciPending=true (same head), so classification runs and throws again each poll. One persistent REST problem therefore starves the whole repository's PR observation. Examples of a persistent problem: a 5xx, logs that have expired (410), or an unexpected job shape.
review-053.failure_scenario: Tracked PR 1 has a timed-out check, and `repos/o/r/commits/<sha>/check-runs` returns 502. PR 2 in the same repo has no CI failure and is then merged. After four poll cycles, `githubPrData(PR2)` is still undefined, so the merge was never recorded. Without the 502 override, the same test records PR 2

review-053.title: Signature line and feed excerpt come from the start of the log, not the failure
review-053.detail: ciSignature picks the first line anywhere in the log that matches error/fail. That can be setup output, or a passing test whose name contains 'error' or 'failed' (runners such as jest --verbose, pytest -v and go test -v print passing test names). The feed excerpt is `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)` of the full log (lines 324 and 507). That is the runner preamble (runner version, OS, image, token permissions), not the failing output. The request's 'failing test or error line' and a useful needs_fix excerpt are not reliably produced. Durations embedded in the line (e.g. `[5000.01ms]`) also make the same flake produce a different signature on each run.
review-053.failure_scenario: For a log whose first lines are `(pass) store > a failed rerun reports needs-fix [3ms]` and then `(fail) smoke > land`, ciSignature returns line="(pass) store > a failed rerun reports needs-fix [3ms]" (checked with bun -e).

review-053.title: Paused (main-red) PRs are fully re-inspected over REST on every poll
review-053.detail: When any check is paused for main red, classifyCi returns false, so ciPending stays true and the whole inspection repeats every 15–45 s. Each repeat fetches the main commit, main check-runs, PR check-runs and statuses. For the PR's other failing checks it also re-downloads the job, annotations and full logs. With several PRs paused during a long main-red episode, this can use up a large share of the 5000/h REST budget.
review-053.failure_scenario: Main stays red on `test` for 2 hours while 10 factory PRs have a failing `test` plus another failing check. That is about 10 PRs × 6+ calls × 80–240 polls/h, which approaches or exceeds the REST rate limit.

review-053.title: Over budget, and a second migration alters a table created in the same change
review-053.detail: The request budgets about 250 changed source lines. The change adds about 545 source lines (ci-classifier.ts alone is 399). The new ci_failures table is created in one migration and then immediately changed by a separate ALTER TABLE migration in the same diff.
review-053.failure_scenario: Not a runtime failure; this is extra maintenance and review cost.

review-054.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
review-054.detail: classifyCi throws on unavailable details, and this await lets that exception escape the repository's observation loop. Later PR snapshots from the already successful GraphQL response are discarded. Persisted ciPending causes the same first PR to throw again every poll, indefinitely starving later PRs when logs remain unavailable. Temporary regression command `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"` logged `Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)` twice; the later PR assertion returned `Expected: "CLOSED" / Received: undefined`.
review-054.failure_scenario: PR #1 has a failed job whose logs return 404, while PR #2 in the same repository closes or merges. Each poll aborts while inspecting #1, so #2's state is never recorded.

review-054.title: Keep newly requested reruns pending until their outcome is observed
review-054.detail: pendingRerun is computed before this inspection requests new reruns, so the function can return true immediately after requesting one. The poller clears ciPending and only resumes inspection when ciKey changes. Because GraphQL fetches only 100 contexts, a rerun outside that page can finish without changing ciKey when another check keeps the rollup red. Its ledger outcome then remains rerunning forever. Temporary regression command `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"` produced `REST calls after invisible rerun: 0` and `Expected: "failed_then_passed" / Received: "rerunning"`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A PR has 101 checks. REST discovers and reruns a timed-out check outside the first 100 GraphQL contexts. It passes at the same SHA, but a visible check remains failed; subsequent polls never reconcile the successful rerun or record flake evidence.

review-054.title: Recognize Node test-runner timeout diagnostics
review-054.detail: The timeout matcher rejects Node's actual diagnostic, `error: 'test timed out after 10ms'`, so an eligible test timeout emits ci.needs_fix without rerunning. A fixture using captured Node TAP output with GitHub-style timestamps reproduces this. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. Output: `Node timeout {"reruns":0,"needsFix":1}`; assertion: `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A factory PR's Actions job finishes with conclusion failure because a Node test exceeds its own timeout; main is green and reruns are enabled.

review-054.title: Record failures in the ledger during main-red pauses
review-054.detail: The main-red branch continues before job/log inspection and recordCiFailure, so these failures never enter the ledger. Pausing per-PR reactions should not discard the requested failure history. Command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts"`. Output: `main red {"ledger":0,"mainRed":1}`; assertion: `Expected length: 1; Received length: 0`.
review-054.failure_scenario: Main and a factory PR fail the same non-security check. If the PR subsequently advances to another SHA before main recovers, its original failure is permanently absent from the ledger.

review-054.title: Main-red failures bypass the failure ledger
review-054.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence, constructing the failure signature, or recording the ledger row. This loses the requested check/error/runner-image/SHA record for these failures. The isolated probe command above produced main-red: {"ledgerRows":0,"posts":0,"feed":["ci.main_red","ci.main_red"]}. If the checks subsequently recover, the original failure is never recorded.
review-054.failure_scenario: A factory PR and main fail the same non-security check. Both later recover before another failing inspection; no ledger row records the PR's original failure signature or SHA.

review-054.title: Playwright security failures can be automatically rerun
review-054.detail: Security detection ignores Playwright failure headings such as `1) [chromium] › tests/security.spec.ts:10:1 › rejects unauthorized access`. In a generic job concluded timed_out, that evidence does not prevent recording the failure and rerunning the job. This violates the security-test exclusion. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed rerun POSTs: 1 ledger rows: 1` and `FAIL Playwright security timeout never reruns ... 1 !== 0`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A generic test job times out and its log contains a Playwright failure heading naming security.spec.ts; the step name is generic and there are no failure annotations.

review-054.title: Indented Playwright timeout diagnostics are not classified as transient
review-054.detail: The Playwright alternative is anchored without allowing leading whitespace. Standard reporter output such as `    Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.` therefore produces ci.needs_fix instead of a rerun. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed rerun POSTs: 0 needs_fix items: 1` and `FAIL indented Playwright timeout is transient ... 0 !== 1`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A GitHub Actions job concludes failure after a Playwright test timeout, with the timeout diagnostic indented in its downloaded log.

review-054.title: Main-red alerts are deduplicated per check instead of per repository
review-054.detail: Each failing check name receives a separate ci.main_red key. When test and lint fail on both main and a PR, two repository items are emitted, contrary to the requested single repository item. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed ci.main_red items: 2` and `FAIL one main-red feed item per repository ... 2 !== 1`.
review-054.failure_scenario: One repository has two checks failing on main and the same two checks failing on a factory PR.

review-054.title: Main-red failures are omitted from the failure ledger
review-054.detail: The main-red branch continues before job inspection and recordCiFailure, so these PR failure signatures, SHAs, runner images, and outcomes are never persisted. Pausing reactions should not discard the requested failure history. Command `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review-probes.ts"` produced `observed main-red ledger rows: 0` and `FAIL main-red PR failures enter the ledger ... 0 !== 1`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A non-security check fails on both main and a factory PR; the PR closes before main recovers, leaving no ledger record of its failure.

review-054.title: Reconciliation loses results when a later attempt reruns another job
review-054.detail: Reconciliation reads only the workflow's latest attempt. Partial job reruns can leave the originating job's completed result in an earlier attempt while the latest attempt contains another job. The missing name is then treated as ambiguous forever, preventing flake recording and further classification. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-sHSr7q/claude-501/ci-review/probe.ts latest`. With the original job succeeding in attempt 2 and another job succeeding in attempt 3, output was `Later unrelated attempt: Ambiguous CI rerun job outcome: rerunning` and `ASSERTION FAILED: a successful rerun in attempt 2 is never read after an unrelated attempt 3`.
review-054.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A from attempt 1; A succeeds in attempt 2. Before the next inspection, another job is rerun in attempt 3. GitHub reports run_attempt=3, whose jobs omit A, leaving A's ledger outcome permanently rerunning despite its successful same-SHA rerun.

review-054.title: Unaccepted rerun requests remain pending forever
review-054.detail: A 429, network failure before submission, or crash between claiming and posting leaves outcome rerun_requested. When GitHub never creates another attempt, reconciliation always continues here, and the pending prior record suppresses ci.needs_fix indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: after 100 reconciliation polls {"complete":false,"posts":1,"outcome":"rerun_requested","needsFix":0}; Expected: true, Received: false.
review-054.failure_scenario: GitHub rejects the rerun with HTTP 429 and run_attempt remains 1, or the daemon crashes after claiming but before sending the POST.

review-054.title: Lagging check data reports a confirmed passing rerun as needing a fix
review-054.detail: Successful reconciliation adds only the new job ID to resolved. If the check-runs endpoint still returns the original failed job, that ID is not skipped. The prior failed_then_passed record prevents another rerun but falls through to needsFix, producing contradictory ledger and feed results. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: successful rerun with lagging checks {"outcome":"failed_then_passed","feed":["ci.needs_fix"]}; Expected: false, Received: true.
review-054.failure_scenario: A pending inspection observes attempt 2 succeeding through the workflow jobs API while GraphQL and the commit check-runs endpoint still expose attempt 1's failure.

review-054.title: Main-red suppression bypasses the failure ledger
review-054.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence, constructing the signature, or recording the failure. Consequently, these failures have no ledger record despite the requirement to record each failure signature, SHA, and outcome. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/ci-review.test.ts". Output: main-red result {"ledgerRows":0,...}; Expected: 1, Received: 0.
review-054.failure_scenario: A factory PR's non-security test job fails while the default branch is red on the same check; ci.main_red is emitted, but ci_failures remains empty.

review-054.title: One CI inspection failure starves later PR observations
review-054.detail: Classifier exceptions escape record and terminate the repository's observation loop. Because ciPending remains persisted, the same PR repeats the failure every poll and prevents later PRs from recording CI, review, closure, or merge observations. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-poller-review.ts"` across three polls saved only `https://github.com/o/r/pull/1`; each poll logged `Incomplete CI inspection: commits/aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa/check-runs?filter=latest&per_page=100&page=1 (404)`.
review-054.failure_scenario: The first tracked PR repeatedly returns unavailable or malformed CI details while a later PR has valid GraphQL observations.

review-054.title: Case-sensitive API URL validation rejects valid repositories
review-054.detail: Repository registration preserves the user's slug casing, while GitHub returns canonical casing in check_run_url. This strict comparison rejects a legitimate job even though the preceding details_url comparison accepts case differences. The rerun reconciliation prefix check has the same problem. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with stored `o/r` and returned `O/R` produced `{"name":"canonical-repo-case","posts":0,"outcomes":[],"needsFix":0,"error":"Error: Incomplete failing job"}`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A repository is registered using lowercase owner/name, but GitHub's canonical owner or repository name contains uppercase characters.

review-054.title: Test timeout classification excludes the requested diagnostic
review-054.detail: Only three hardcoded diagnostic formats qualify. An actual failure line such as `error: smoke timed out after 30000ms` is classified as needs-fix despite matching the requested test timeout case. The added tests explicitly expect this exclusion. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` produced `{"name":"test-own-timeout","posts":0,"outcomes":["failed"],"needsFix":4,"error":""}`.
review-054.failure_scenario: A test runner reports its own timeout as `error: smoke timed out after 30000ms` and the Actions job concludes failure.

review-054.title: Main-branch status lookup depends on the PR's context types
review-054.detail: The shared checks function fetches legacy commit statuses only when the PR snapshot contains StatusContext entries or is truncated. Consequently, a failing main status is invisible when the PR exposes the same check through CheckRun. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/ci-review.ts"` with a failing main status named test produced `{"name":"main-red-legacy-status","posts":1,"mainStatusReads":0,"outcomes":["rerunning"],"needsFix":0,"error":""}`.
review-054.failure_scenario: Main reports a failing legacy commit status named test, while the factory PR reports test through the Checks API.

review-054.title: Later partial attempts strand tracked rerun results
review-054.detail: Reconciliation searches only the latest workflow attempt. GitHub partial reruns can omit jobs completed in earlier attempts, so a later rerun of another job makes the tracked job disappear from this query permanently. Every subsequent inspection throws instead of recording its result. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a tracked rerun is reconciled after a later partial attempt: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job`.
review-054.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A from attempt 1; A passes in attempt 2. Before polling, another failed job B is rerun in attempt 3, whose jobs response contains only B.

review-054.title: Main-red failures bypass the failure ledger
review-054.detail: The main-red branch continues before job inspection and recordCiFailure, so these PR failures never receive the required signature, runner image, SHA, and outcome record. Pausing reactions should not discard failure evidence. Running `bun /private/tmp/lr-MP54Mh/claude-501/ci-review.ts` produced `FAIL a main-red failure is still recorded in the failure ledger` with `0 !== 1`.
review-054.failure_scenario: Both the default branch and a factory PR fail the non-security check 'test'; the classifier emits ci.main_red but creates no ledger row for the PR failure.

review-054.title: Isolate CI inspection failures to the affected PR
review-054.detail: A classifier exception escapes record(), aborting observation of every later PR in the repository. A persistent missing log therefore starves unrelated PRs indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: starvation {"secondSnapshot":null,"logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Incomplete CI inspection: actions/jobs/21/logs (404)"]}; assertion expected secondSnapshot not to be null.
review-054.failure_scenario: Two tracked PRs share a repository. The first has a failed job whose logs return 404. The second never receives a saved observation, including subsequent merge, close, review, or CI changes.

review-054.title: Resolve claims when rate limiting rejects the rerun
review-054.detail: A rejected HTTP 429 leaves rerun_requested permanently claimed. Because no rerun actually started, run_attempt never advances; reconciliation neither retries nor emits ci.needs_fix. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output after cooldown and eight further polls: rate-limited claim {"outcome":"rerun_requested","reruns":1,"needsFix":0}; assertion expected outcome not to remain rerun_requested.
review-054.failure_scenario: GitHub returns 429 to the rerun POST, then becomes available again. The workflow remains on its original failed attempt forever, with no rerun or needs-fix result.

review-054.title: Search intervening attempts when reconciling a rerun
review-054.detail: Reconciliation examines only the latest workflow attempt. Attempt-specific job listings omit jobs that were not rerun in that attempt, so a subsequent partial rerun can permanently hide the factory's completed attempt. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: partial-rerun {"outcome":"rerunning","logs":["GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job","GitHub poll of o/r failed: Error: Ambiguous CI rerun job"]}; expected failed_then_passed.
review-054.failure_scenario: The factory reruns job A in attempt 2 and it passes. Before the next poll, someone reruns unrelated job B in attempt 3. The classifier never reads A's passing attempt and keeps its ledger row pending.

review-054.title: Observe rerun completion beyond the first 100 contexts
review-054.detail: An outstanding rerun triggers inspection only when ciChanged is true. The query observes just the first 100 contexts, while REST can discover and rerun checks outside that page. Completion of such a check can leave ciKey unchanged indefinitely. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: hidden rerun {"outcome":"rerunning","additionalRestCalls":0}; expected failed_then_passed.
review-054.failure_scenario: A PR has 101 checks. A visible check keeps the rollup red, and the hidden check is rerun successfully. Neither the first 100 contexts nor the rollup changes, so the passing rerun is never recorded.

review-054.title: Recognize standard security-test failure diagnostics
review-054.detail: The security exclusion misses standard Go failure lines such as '--- FAIL: TestSecurity (0.00s)'. A generic timed-out job containing that failure is rerun and entered in the ledger, violating the security-test exclusion. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: security reruns {"reruns":1,"ledger":[..."outcome":"rerunning"...]}; assertion expected zero reruns.
review-054.failure_scenario: A job named test times out after reporting a failed TestSecurity test. Its steps have generic names and there are no annotations. The classifier automatically reruns the security failure.

review-054.title: Record failures suppressed by red main in the ledger
review-054.detail: The main-red branch continues before fetching job evidence or recording the failure. These failures never receive the requested signature, runner image, SHA, or outcome in the ledger. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-ci.test.ts". Output: main-red ledger []; assertion expected length 1, received length 0.
review-054.failure_scenario: A factory PR fails the same check as main. The repository notification is emitted, but its failure is absent from the ledger; pushing a new SHA before main recovers loses the observation permanently.

review-054.title: A CI classification error on one PR aborts observation of all later PRs in the repo, permanently if the error is deterministic
review-054.detail: classifyCi throws on any unexpected REST shape or inconsistency, for example a zod parse failure, "Ambiguous originating CI job", "Incomplete failing check", "Outdated CI check completion" or an annotation count mismatch. Nothing in record() catches the exception, so it propagates out of observe(), and the rest of the batch loop is abandoned. Because ciPending is persisted as true and survives while the head is the same (`same && prev?.ciPending`), the same PR throws again on every poll. The later PRs in that repository are therefore starved indefinitely: no merged/closed/ci events and no reconcile.
review-054.failure_scenario: I reproduced this with a temporary test in a TMPDIR copy that used pollerHarness. PR o/r#1's rollup turns FAILURE, and `repos/o/r/commits/main` returns 200 `{sha:"unexpected"}`, which fails zod. PR o/r#2 is then merged. After 10 poll cycles, `store.getRun(run2.id).merged` was still false and the log

review-054.title: Observations are now discarded entirely whenever observePrHead refuses, including while a push is in progress or left stuck
review-054.detail: Before this change, record() ignored observePrHead's result and always saved the snapshot and its feed items. Now `if (!store.observePrHead(...)) return undefined;` drops the whole observation whenever the version moved or pushingTo(prUrl) is true. pushingTo stays true until the pushing run is terminal, and the store's own comment says "a crash can leave one behind". During that window the poller never records merges, closes, comments or CI changes for the PR. Only classifyCi needs to be gated on the head being current.

review-054.detail: `classifyCi` throws on any incomplete REST evidence: a non-200 log, annotation, job or commit read; a zod parse failure; 'Incomplete failing check'; or 'Ambiguous originating CI job'. `record()` doesn't catch it. The exception escapes `observe()`, which `tick` catches per repository, so every PR after the failing one in that batch goes unrecorded. `ciPending` is saved as true before the call, and `same && prev.ciPending` keeps it true. review-054.title: Main-red pause re-fetches REST on every poll, though the request limits fetching to GraphQL changes
review-054.detail: When a PR's failing check is red on main, `classifyCi` returns `!paused` = false. `record()` then returns null with `ciPending` still true, so the next poll reclassifies with no GraphQL change. Each pass reads the main commit, main's check-runs and the PR's check-runs. Main's checks are fetched again for every PR rather than once per repository, and this continues for as long as main stays red, possibly hours or days. The request says 'Fetch the failing check runs and jobs by REST, only when the GraphQL state changed.' Because `record` returns null, the mergeability nudge is also skipped and the repository's access-problem clear never runs while paused.

review-054.title: Ledger signatures include per-run noise, so the same flake never matches across occurrences
review-054.detail: `ciSignature` uses the first log line matching `/timed out after|##[error]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i`, verbatim apart from a leading timestamp, as the error line. That keeps volatile content such as Bun's duration suffix. It also matches incidental setup lines (e.g. `fail-fast: true`) that print before the real failure. The flake ledger exists to record each failure signature so recurring nondeterminism can be recognised, and these signatures differ on every occurrence.

A log with `  fail-fast: true` before `error: real problem` gives t

review-054.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` sets `excerpt = quote(log.trim().slice(0, 2000))`. A real Actions job log starts with runner setup output (runner version, OS, image, checkout), so the first 2000 characters almost never contain the failure. The excerpt is noise, and the failing lines that sit past 2000 characters are dropped.

review-054.title: Ad-hoc '> ' quoting instead of the codebase's untrusted-data convention
review-054.detail: Untrusted GitHub text elsewhere goes through `quotedJson`, or is labelled with an explicit 'untrusted … quoted data' preface (`src/integrations/github.ts:48`, `src/pipeline/triage-decisions.ts`). This change adds a separate `> `-prefix scheme plus an `untrusted: true` flag. That satisfies the letter of the requirement but is inconsistent with the existing approach, and it doesn't escape angle brackets or tags if feed data is later embedded in a tagged prompt.

review-054.title: About twice the stated budget, with dense and hard-to-audit control flow
review-054.detail: The request budgets about 250 changed source lines. The diff adds about 560 source lines, 411 of them in a single `classifyCi` function with many nested closures, several throw-to-retry paths, and two migrations for one new table. The first migration creates `ci_failures` and the second immediately ALTERs it; neither file has shipped, so they could be one. This complexity makes the reliability problems above (throw semantics, pending loops) easy to miss.

review-054.detail: `/…|sast|dast|vulnerab/i` has no word boundaries, so 'disaster', 'podcast' (no) or 'sastisfy'-style tokens count as security evidence. That suppresses both the rerun and the ledger row. The effect is conservative but surprising.
