review-054.title: A persistent classifier exception on one PR starves every later PR in the repo batch, merges included
review-054.detail: `classifyCi` throws on many conditions (`Incomplete CI inspection` for any non-200 status, `Incomplete failing check`, `Ambiguous originating CI job`, `Outdated CI check completion`, and so on). It runs inside `record()`, which runs inside the `for (const [i, pr] of known.entries())` loop in `observe()`. The throw unwinds `observe()`, which `tick` catches per repository, so no later PR in that batch is recorded. The PR that threw was already saved with `ciPending: true`, and `(same && prev?.ciPending)` keeps it pending, so the same throw recurs on every poll. The starvation lasts until that PR's head or CI changes. The base code had no such path.

review-054.title: Main-red pause re-fetches REST on every poll although GraphQL is unchanged
review-054.detail: When a PR's failing check is red on main, `classifyCi` returns false (`paused`). `ciPending` therefore stays persisted, and every later poll re-runs the classification: GET commits/main, the main check-runs pages, and the PR check-runs pages, even when the GraphQL `ciKey` is identical. The request says to fetch failing check runs and jobs by REST "only when the GraphQL state changed". Delivered PRs poll every 15 s, which is roughly 720 or more REST calls per hour per paused PR. Several PRs blocked by one red main can use up the 5000/h budget that the poller and the rest of the factory share.
review-054.failure_scenario: Probe test: one PR fails `test` and main's check `test` is also failing. After the first poll there were 4 REST calls. After 10 more polls with unchanged GraphQL there were 34: commits/main, main check-runs and PR check-runs on every cycle.

review-054.title: Failure signature can pick a passing test or setup line, and it includes run timings
review-054.detail: `ciSignature` takes the first log line matching `/timed out after|##\[error\]|\b(?:error|fail(?:ed|ure)?)\b/i`. Passing test names containing 'error' or 'fail', and action inputs such as `continue-on-error: false` or `fail-on-cache-miss`, match before the actual failure. Lines also keep durations such as `[5000.01ms]`, so the same failure produces a different signature on every run. The ledger's "failing test or error line" is then wrong, unrelated failures in one job collapse into one signature (the cap is over-applied, and needs_fix items are deduplicated away), and identical failures never aggregate across runs.

review-054.title: Fail-fast cancelled matrix jobs are treated as transient, rerun, and recorded as flakes
review-054.detail: Any check or job with conclusion `cancelled` is classified as transient, unless the remote head has moved. The request covers a *run* cancelled without being superseded. In a matrix with fail-fast, a real failure in one job cancels its siblings at the same SHA. Those cancelled siblings get rerun, and when the rerun passes, `failed_then_passed` is written to the ledger as nondeterminism evidence, although nothing was nondeterministic. The rerun budget is also spent for nothing. The test 'eligible cancelled failure reruns only its job' locks this behaviour in.

review-054.detail: The base code called `store.observePrHead(pr.url, head, since)` and still saved the snapshot and emitted feed items. The change returns early when that call returns false, which happens while a round is pushing or when the version has moved. During that window pr.merged, pr.closed, review and comment events for the PR are not recorded. This change in behaviour is outside the CI scope and is untested.

review-054.title: Feed excerpt is the first 2000 chars of the job log (runner setup), not the failure
review-054.detail: `emit(..., log || f.line)` passes the whole job log, and `excerpt.trim().slice(0, 2000)` keeps its head. GitHub Actions job logs begin with runner, image and setup output, so for any realistic log the excerpt contains no failure information.

review-054.detail: Each eligible job gets its own POST to `actions/jobs/{id}/rerun`. After the first one, the run is in progress again, and GitHub may refuse a second job rerun on a running run. A 4xx response is treated as a definitive `rerun_rejected` followed by needs_fix. The request says "Rerun the failed jobs", and `runs/{id}/rerun-failed-jobs` does that in one call. I could not verify GitHub's live behaviour here.

review-056.detail: Probe results have no generation or ordering guard. Disabling and re-enabling a provider starts another probe, but the previous probe can finish afterward and replace the newer served list in memory and SQLite. review-056.title: PATCH cannot clear a runtime model's default effort
review-056.detail: `patch` merges `{...old, ...patch}` and runs the result through `mapFields`. That step drops `undefined` but keeps `null`, and `modelSchema.effort` is `.optional()`, so `{effort: null}` is rejected. JSON has no way to send `undefined`, so a default effort, once set, can only be removed by deleting and re-adding the model. Deletion is itself blocked while any policy cell names the model. review-057.detail: On startup the Factory constructor throws on any stored runtime model whose id collides with a code or config model, or whose provider no longer exists. Removing or renaming the provider in config.toml throws 'unknown provider'. The only supported removal path, `limitless catalog remove`, is an HTTP call to the daemon that just failed to start, so recovery means editing SQLite by hand. review-057.title: PATCH cannot clear a runtime model's default effort
review-057.detail: `patch` merges `{...old, ...patch}` and re-validates with `modelSchema`. `effort` is `z.enum(...).optional()`, so `effort: null` fails validation, and JSON has no way to send `undefined`. Once a default effort is set it can only be changed to another member of `efforts`. You can't remove it, and you can't narrow `efforts` below it. The workaround is delete and re-add, which DELETE refuses while any policy cell names the model. The GUIDE says agent roles on local Claude-backed servers should omit the default effort, so this is a realistic edit.
review-057.failure_scenario: Runtime model with efforts [none,high] and effort none. `PATCH {efforts:["high"]}` fails with 'model.effort: absent from efforts'. `PATCH {efforts:["high"], effort:null}` fails with 'model.effort: invalid or missing field'. I confirmed both with a throwaway test.

review-057.title: Smoke now silently drops checks for disabled providers and opens the production DB
review-057.detail: `main()` now opens `new Store(cfg.paths.db)`, which runs migrations against the live database, and filters every provider through `getProviderEnabledOverride`. `backendChecks` changed from throwing on a missing provider to `continue` / `return checks`. A provider the operator disabled at runtime (claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter, typesafe) therefore gets no check and no skip row in the deploy smoke report. That is an unrequested change to the deploy gate: a broken provider that is temporarily disabled passes the smoke check and fails once it is re-enabled. Only the catalog check needed the runtime models.
review-057.failure_scenario: Operator runs `limitless providers disable codex`. Deploy smoke runs no codex checks at all, and the report has no codex rows.

That is every minute for every probed provider even when nothing changed, and twice when health changes, because `setHealthy`→`persist` already publishes. Each publish also triggers `publishFeed()`. `status()` now runs two SQLite queries through `discovery()`, and it is called per candidate on the invoke hot path (`tracker.status(t.provider)` in context.ts).

review-057.title: Daemon fails to start when a stored runtime model collides with a code/config model or its provider is gone
review-057.detail:
Factory's constructor loads `store.runtimeModels()` and throws `catalog collision: ` or `unknown provider

` for any stored row that no longer fits the static catalog. The collision check exists at add time, but the static catalog can change later: config.toml edits, a code release that adds the same id, or a provider removed from config. When it does, the whole factory refuses to boot. `limitless catalog remove` goes through the HTTP API, so it can't be used while the daemon is down. The operator's only fix is to edit the `runtime_models` table by hand. Stored rows are also not re-validated (no `runtimeModel()` pass) on load. No test covers a restart after the static catalog changes.

review-057.title: DELETE checks only operator cells; deleting a model the evals policy layer names empties live routing and breaks the next restart
review-057.detail: `remove()` scans only `store.routingCells()`. The effective policy (`router.getPolicy()`) also contains the evals layer read from policyPath. Runtime models are loaded before `readPolicy`, so that file can legitimately name one. Deletion is then allowed. The live cell keeps pointing at a missing id, so that role gets no candidates. On the next boot, `readPolicy` rejects the file with `unknown model ID` and the Factory fails to start.

review-069.title: A blocked land stays in the digest after the PR is merged, closed or the run is resolved

Bidi controls (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters (U+200B–U+200F, U+FEFF) pass through unescaped into the session context, so a hostile PR title can visually reorder or hide text inside the quotes.

review-070.title: Digest lines have no length cap, so one long question or title can flood session context
review-070.detail: Each row prints the full quoted title and summary; for questions, the summary is replaced with the full open question text. JSON quoting keeps a row on one line, so the 20-line limit holds. But nothing limits how long a row is. Output from a SessionStart hook goes into the agent's context, so a multi-kilobyte question or a long PR title (untrusted text) produces a very large digest.
review-070.failure_scenario: A run asks a 5 KB clarification question. Every new session's digest injects all 5 KB into the context.

review-070.title: Digest makes one or two HTTP calls per distinct run with no limit
review-070.detail: For every distinct run in the candidate groups, the digest fetches `/api/runs/:id`, and also `/api/land?run=` when the run has a PR. Those calls happen one after another. The hook's `claude` consumer is never acknowledged by the digest itself and may not match the consumer the agent acks with. In that case the cursor stays at 0, the whole retained feed is rescanned at every session start, and the number of calls grows with the history.
review-070.failure_scenario: An install with several hundred runs that have PRs never acks the `claude` consumer. Each SessionStart makes hundreds of sequential requests and may approach the hook timeout.

review-070.title: Approval row is read twice in getRunDetail
review-070.detail: `approvalFor` already runs `SELECT ... FROM review_approvals WHERE pr_url = ? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1`. The new code runs the same query again only to get `created_at`. The source change is also about 380 lines against a budget of about 200.
review-070.failure_scenario: There is no functional failure; this is a duplicate query and extra code.

review-070.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag

Output: PR state unknown; error: Expected Landed (exit 1).

review-070.detail: The review predicate ignores review.rounds. review-070.title: MCP review verdicts are recorded with reviewer "human"
review-070.detail: limitless_review passes the verdict without a reviewer, so submitReview falls back to `parsed.data.reviewer ?? "human"`. An approval an AI agent submits over MCP is stored in review_approvals, and announced in the review.approved feed item, as "approved ... by human". This differs from the other provenance in this code: the CLI sets reviewer to $USER, and MCP answers pass by: "mcp". The approval record is what authorizes a land, so this misattribution weakens the audit trail.
review-070.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_review with verdict=approve. review_approvals.reviewer = 'human' and the feed shows 'approved at <sha> by human', even though no human approved.

review-070.title: Digest lists PRs with an in-flight review round as awaiting review
review-070.detail: The "PRs awaiting review" filter only checks for a missing or stale approval and the land state. It never looks at review.rounds. After a `changes` verdict, the approval is marked stale and a round run is queued. The pr_opened item for that PR then still passes the filter, so the digest asks the user to review a PR the factory is still reworking. limitless_status does handle this case ("Review changes in progress"), so the two outputs disagree.
review-070.failure_scenario: A run opens PR #5, and the reviewer submits verdict=changes, which queues round 1. A new session's digest still shows PR #5 under 'PRs awaiting review' until the round delivers.

review-070.title: Digest item lines are unbounded in width
review-070.detail: Each row includes the full quoted title and summary. For questions, the summary is replaced with the full open-question text. The output is capped at 20 lines, but a single line can carry kilobytes of untrusted text into every session's context through the SessionStart hook.

review-070.title: Codex skill tells Codex to use the 'claude' feed consumer
review-070.detail: The Codex skill is a verbatim copy of the Claude skill and recommends `limitless digest --consumer claude`. If Codex uses that consumer for its inbox, it shares a feed cursor with Claude Code, so acks from one hide items from the other.
review-070.failure_scenario: Codex follows the skill, then reads and acks through consumer 'claude'. Claude Code's next digest silently skips those items.

review-070.title: MCP review verdicts are attributed to reviewer "human"
review-070.detail: The limitless_review tool sends {verdict, reviewedSha, findings} with no reviewer. submitReview defaults the reviewer to "human" (src/pipeline/review-round.ts:193), so approvals an agent makes through MCP are stored in review_approvals as human approvals. The review.approved feed summary then says "by human". The existing answer tool tags its writes with by: "mcp", but the review path doesn't.
review-070.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_review with verdict approve. The approval row and feed item say the PR was approved by "human", which misleads anyone auditing who approved what landed.

review-070.title: Digest lists PRs with an in-flight review round as "awaiting review"
review-070.detail: For the PR group, an item counts as actionable when there is no current approval and no active land. It never looks at detail.review.rounds. After a reviewer requests changes, the approval is marked stale and a round run starts. The digest keeps listing that PR under "PRs awaiting review" while the factory is still making the changes. explainStatus handles the same case correctly ("Review changes in progress"), so the two summaries disagree.
review-070.failure_scenario: A run opens a PR and the reviewer calls limitless_review with verdict changes, which creates a round that is now running. The next session's digest shows the PR under "PRs awaiting review" and prompts another review of a head that is about to change.

review-070.title: One failed per-run lookup aborts the whole session digest
review-070.detail: For each item, the digest calls /api/runs/:id and /api/land?run= one after another, with no error handling. If any lookup returns an error, for example a 400 from land.list throwing "run not found" or a transient failure, digestCommand throws and prints nothing. That includes the counts and the other categories. Reading a long-unread feed also means two sequential requests per distinct run at every session start.
review-070.failure_scenario: The feed has an item whose run lookup fails. The SessionStart hook exits non-zero with only an error message, so the session gets no digest at all.

Because blocked entries persist, status continues recommending another landing request after the work has been resolved. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-probes.ts". For a resolved run with a CLOSED PR, output includes "state":"Landing blocked" and "nextAction":"Inspect the land reason, resolve the blocker, then request limitless_land again." The landing API rejects closed PRs.
review-071.failure_scenario: Landing blocks, the PR is closed, and the run is resolved as pr_closed. limitless_status still instructs the agent to queue landing again.

review-071.title: Honor the run's persisted merge flag
review-071.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the landed condition never checks it. Existing delivery paths persist merged=true without recording a merged PR snapshot or land entry, so status can describe a confirmed merge as unknown or awaiting review. Boundary command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts". Output: FAIL persisted merged run: expected "Landed", got "PR state unknown".
review-071.failure_scenario: Delivery successfully merges under the auto policy and stores run.merged=true; GitHub polling is disabled or has not saved a merged observation, and there is no land entry.

review-071.title: Let a closed PR supersede a historical landing blocker
review-071.detail: The blocked-land branch runs before the CLOSED PR check. After someone closes a blocked PR, status still instructs the agent to resolve the blocker and request limitless_land again, although the landing API rejects closed PRs. Boundary command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts". Output: FAIL closed PR with historical blocked land: expected "PR closed", got "Landing blocked".
review-071.failure_scenario: A land blocks on CI, then the PR is closed without merging and its CLOSED observation is saved.

review-071.title: Exclude PRs whose review fixes are still in progress
review-071.detail: The review eligibility predicate ignores review.rounds. An unread PR-opened event remains eligible after a changes verdict queues a review round, so the digest asks for review before the requested fixes are delivered. Boundary command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-boundaries.ts". Output: FAIL PR undergoing queued review fixes: expected "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0", got "Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0".
review-071.failure_scenario: The consumer has not acknowledged the original PR-opened event, and a changes verdict has created a queued or running review round on that PR.

review-071.title: limitless_status omits state and nextAction when the private-strings policy cannot be loaded
review-071.detail: When loadPrivateStrings() throws, result() returns only {land:{id,state}, openQuestions}. The response then has no run id, no plain-language state and no next action, which the request says the tool must return. Every state and nextAction string is a fixed literal, apart from interpolated land-state enum values and run IDs, so they could be returned safely even without the policy.
review-071.failure_scenario: ~/.config/limitless/private-strings.txt is unreadable or not valid UTF-8. limitless_status then returns {land:null, openQuestions:0}, and the agent gets no state or next action.

review-071.title: Digest lists an approved PR as awaiting review when the PR head has never been observed
review-071.detail: The review group is actionable when `approval.sha !== pr?.headRefOid`. If no PR snapshot is saved, headRefOid is undefined, so an approved PR with a current approval still appears under 'PRs awaiting review'. A test ('keeps a newly delivered unobserved PR eligible') shows this is a deliberate choice for unobserved PRs. Still, it reports a valid approval as review-needed, whereas limitless_status reports 'PR state unknown' for the same state.
review-071.failure_scenario: A run has a non-stale approval, but the GitHub poller has not saved a snapshot yet. The digest counts it under 'PRs awaiting review'.

review-071.title: Digest lines have no length cap, so 20 lines can still carry a lot of untrusted text
review-071.detail: Each row includes the full quoted title and summary, such as question text or a run error. The output stays within 20 lines, but one line can be very long and is injected into the session context at SessionStart.
review-071.failure_scenario: A run question or error several KB long is printed in full on a single digest line at session start.

review-071.title: limitless_status leaves out state and nextAction when the privacy policy fails to load
review-071.detail: If loadPrivateStrings throws (for example, private-strings.txt is unreadable or sits inside a repository), result() returns only {land:{id,state}, openQuestions}. The run id, the plain-language state and nextAction are all gone, and nothing tells the agent the response was cut down. The state and nextAction strings are fixed templates plus enum values and run ids that the server generates. They could still be returned safely; only land.reason needs to be dropped.
review-071.failure_scenario: ~/.config/limitless/private-strings.txt is unreadable or not valid UTF-8. Calling limitless_status on any run returns {land:null, openQuestions:0} with no state or next action.

review-071.title: Digest lists PRs as awaiting review while a changes round is still running
review-071.detail: The 'PRs awaiting review' check looks only at whether an approval exists and is fresh, and at the land state. Requesting changes marks the approval stale and starts a round run. Until that round delivers, the PR still counts as awaiting review, even though the factory is working on it. limitless_status handles this case and reports 'Review changes in progress', so the two commands disagree.
review-071.failure_scenario: The feed since the cursor contains run.pr_opened for run A. The reviewer then submits a 'changes' verdict and round run B is running. The digest shows A's PR under 'PRs awaiting review', while limitless_status says changes are in progress.

review-071.title: One failed detail or land lookup aborts the whole digest
review-071.detail: Digest fetches /api/runs/:id and /api/land?run= one item at a time, with no per-item error handling. If any single run lookup fails (the run was removed, or a transient error), the SessionStart hook prints nothing useful and exits with an error. With a large backlog it also makes many requests one after another at session start.
review-071.failure_scenario: The feed holds an item whose runId now returns 404. `limitless digest` throws and prints no counts at all.

review-072.title: Privacy-policy failure now hides results of every existing MCP tool, including mutations
review-072.detail: Every tool output now goes through loadOutputPrivacy(). If private-strings.txt cannot be read, every tool except status returns only {message: 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.'}. That includes create_run, cancel_run, answer_question, review and land, which still carry out the mutation. The caller loses the created run id or the land entry and cannot tell whether the call worked, which invites a duplicate retry. Before this change these existing tools returned their results.

review-072.title: limitless_status returns no state or nextAction when the privacy policy is unavailable
review-072.detail: In the no-privacy branch, result() returns only {land:{id,state}, openQuestions} and drops `state` and `nextAction`, which are the tool's whole purpose. Both strings are hard-coded enum-like text, apart from the `round.runId` and `land.state` parts that are interpolated into them. The tool description does not mention this degraded shape.

review-072.title: Digest quoting does not escape bidi or zero-width characters in untrusted PR titles
review-072.detail: quote() uses JSON.stringify and also escapes U+007F–U+009F and U+2028/2029. Bidi overrides (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) and zero-width characters pass through unchanged. A PR title can visually reorder or hide parts of the quoted line in the terminal and in the SessionStart context, which weakens the 'quoted untrusted text' guarantee.

review-072.title: Approved PRs with no saved PR snapshot are listed as awaiting review
review-072.detail: The check `approval.sha !== pr?.headRefOid` is true whenever prSnapshot is missing, so a PR with a valid, non-stale approval and no saved observation is counted under 'PRs awaiting review'. limitless_status reports the same PR as 'PR state unknown', so the two outputs disagree.
review-072.failure_scenario: The PR was approved through limitless_review before the GitHub poller saved a snapshot. The digest shows it as awaiting review, and a new session reviews it again.

review-072.title: Unrequested change to the private-string gate decoder, and the change exceeds the ~200-line budget
review-072.detail: The publication gate now decodes `\uXXXX` escapes in every scanned text, not only in the new MCP and digest output. This is stricter, so false positives become more likely in code that contains literal Unicode escapes. It falls outside the requested scope. Together with the new privacy layer applied to every MCP tool, source changes total about 450 lines against a budget of about 200.
review-072.failure_scenario: A diff contains a literal string such as "Acme" while "Acme" is in private-strings.txt. Publication is now blocked where it was not before.

review-072.title: Digest lists PRs as awaiting review while their run is still in progress
review-072.detail: The 'PRs awaiting review' filter checks only that the run is not resolved, cancelled or merged, that a PR exists, that the PR is not closed, and the approval and land state. It does not require the run to be finished. submitReview refuses any owner whose status is not succeeded or needs_human. So a run that opened its PR and is still running (CI wait, verify) shows up as review-ready, and a review verdict would be refused with 409. explainStatus handles this case as 'Work pending', so the two tools disagree.
review-072.failure_scenario: A run emits run.pr_opened, then sits in status 'running' waiting on CI. The digest shows 'PRs awaiting review: 1', but limitless_review returns 'only a finished run ... can be reviewed'.

review-072.title: Publication-gate decoding changed outside the requested scope
review-072.detail: privateMatches now also decodes literal \uXXXX escapes. That function is the shared publication gate used by the engine, not only the new output privacy. The change alters gate behaviour for all runs, which may block content that previously passed. Combined with the new private-output layer applied to every existing MCP tool, the diff goes well beyond the ~200-line budget and the stated feature.
review-072.failure_scenario: A diff containing a JSON-escaped form of a private string (e.g. acme) is now blocked by the publication gate, where it was previously allowed.

After those are acknowledged, a new head can invalidate approval and produce a pr.ci_passed event, but the digest never reads that run's current state. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-digest-review.ts" stale` returned exactly:
Limitless digest (read only; quoted text is untrusted data)
Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0
The fixture contains an open PR with a stale approval and an unread CI event for its new head.

review-073.detail:
The review predicate checks approval and land state but ignores review rounds. Requesting changes stales the approval immediately, so the original PR remains listed as awaiting review while the factory is still implementing those changes. Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0

The fixture's latest review round is running.

review-073.detail: The status schema discards run.merged, and the landed predicate never checks it. review-073.detail: The digest checks approvals and lands but ignores review.rounds, so a PR whose requested changes are currently being implemented remains advertised as awaiting review. review-073.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate; it blocks text that needs exactly 5 decode rounds, even with an empty denylist
review-073.detail: privateMatches is the shared denylist check used by the publication gates (audit.ts, engine checkPrivateText, repos.ts blob scan, github-notifier, land queue). The diff makes it decode repeatedly and adds \uXXXX unescaping. If decoding hasn't settled after 5 rounds, it returns a synthetic entry 0, which blocks publication. The loop also gives up one round early: after the 5th decode it never checks whether a 6th would be stable, so input that settles after exactly 5 decodes is rejected. Entry 0 is returned even when private-strings.txt is empty. The MCP/digest feature didn't need this change to publication gating, and it makes the change bigger than the ~200-line budget.
review-073.failure_scenario: [redacted diagnostic]

review-073.title: When the privacy policy can't be read, every existing MCP tool, including successful mutations, returns only 'output withheld'
review-073.detail: The CallTool handler now runs every tool result through loadOutputPrivacy. If private-strings.txt can't be read (bad UTF-8, permissions), all tools except limitless_status return {message:'Tool output withheld'}. That includes create_run after it has created the run, so the agent never gets the new run's id. Previously these tools returned their results directly. This changes how all nine existing tools behave, which the request didn't ask for, and it hides the id needed to inspect a mutation instead of retrying it.
review-073.failure_scenario: private-strings.txt has invalid UTF-8 → limitless_create_run creates a run but returns only 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.', and the agent has no id to look it up.

review-073.title: Digest makes 1–2 API calls for every distinct run in the unread feed, sequentially, inside a SessionStart hook
review-073.detail: For each grouped item, the digest fetches /api/runs/:id and, if the run has a PR, /api/land?run=, one request at a time. If the consumer has never acked (the suggested hook uses --consumer claude), the cursor is at 0 and every retained run with a question, failure, PR or review event is fetched one by one, which slows session start.
review-073.failure_scenario: A fresh 'claude' consumer with a few hundred retained run/PR events triggers several hundred sequential HTTP requests before the session starts.

review-073.title: Approved PRs with no saved head observation are counted as awaiting review
review-073.detail: `approval.sha !== pr?.headRefOid` is true when there is no prSnapshot, so a PR with a fresh valid approval is still listed under 'PRs awaiting review'. In the same case limitless_status reports 'PR state unknown', so the two outputs disagree.
review-073.failure_scenario: The PR was approved but the poller hasn't saved a snapshot yet; the digest lists it as needing review.

review-073.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate now blocks on deep encoding even with an empty denylist
review-073.detail: `privateMatches` now repeatedly decodes `%xx` and literal `\uXXXX` escapes. After 5 rounds it returns a synthetic entry 0, and that entry is returned even when `private-strings.txt` is empty. `audit.ts` (every added diff line) and `repos.ts` (blob scanning) both consume this, so an MCP/digest feature now changes when publication is blocked for every run. This is outside the scope of the request (MCP tools and digest) and roughly doubles the size of the diff in security-sensitive code.
review-073.failure_scenario: [redacted diagnostic]

review-073.title: Short registered credentials cause substring withholding of whole MCP output fields
review-073.detail: `loadOutputPrivacy` passes every registered credential to `privateMatches`, which does a case-insensitive substring match. `redactCredentials` deliberately skips substring redaction for secrets under 8 characters to avoid false positives. The new path bypasses that guard and replaces the entire field with `[withheld: private text]`. Because `createMcpServer` now applies this to the output of every tool (including keys), existing tools such as get_run and feed are affected as well as the new ones.
review-073.failure_scenario: A config secret with a short value (e.g. 'run' or '1234') is registered. Every MCP response string containing that substring, such as run IDs or statuses, comes back as `[withheld: private text]`. I confirmed `privateMatches('run-123 status running', [{value:'run',entry:0}])` matches.

review-073.title: Digest makes up to two sequential HTTP requests per distinct run in the SessionStart hook
review-073.detail: After paging the whole feed since the cursor, the digest fetches `/api/runs/:id` and `/api/land?run=` sequentially for every distinct run across all three groups. A consumer that has never acknowledged (the default `claude` consumer in the suggested hook) scans the whole retained feed. That can mean hundreds of serial requests before the session starts.
review-073.failure_scenario: A fresh consumer with 300 retained feed items across 150 runs makes about 300 serial requests every time a Claude Code session starts.

review-073.title: GET /api/land?run=<unknown> throws a generic Error and likely returns 500 instead of 404
review-073.detail: `list(runId)` throws `new Error("run not found")`. The HTTP handler has no mapping for it, unlike the other run routes, which return `error("run not found", 404)`.
review-073.failure_scenario: `curl /api/land?run=nope` responds with a server error rather than 404.

review-073.title: limitless_status gives no state or next action when the privacy policy cannot be read
review-073.detail: When `loadOutputPrivacy()` returns null, `explainStatus` returns only `{land, openQuestions}` and drops `state` and `nextAction`. Those are generated, constant strings that contain no untrusted text, so the tool loses its purpose for no privacy benefit.

review-073.title: Unread PR updates can hide a newly stale approval
review-073.detail: Review candidates are collected only from PR-opened, round-delivered and approved events. review-073.detail: The review predicate ignores review.rounds. A PR whose requested changes are still running is presented as awaiting another review. review-073.title: Honor the run's confirmed merged flag
review-073.detail: The status schema discards run.merged, and the landed check never consults it. Existing auto-merge delivery records merged:true without requiring a land entry or saved PR snapshot, so status can incorrectly tell the agent to await observations after delivery already confirmed the merge. review-073.detail: The status schema strips run.merged, and the terminal-state check never examines it. review-073.detail: The current-state filter checks approval and landing state but ignores review.rounds. review-073.failure_scenario: The consumer has not acknowledged the original PR-opened event, requests changes, and starts a new session while the resulting review round is running. The digest incorrectly presents the PR as ready for another review.

review-073.title: Reconcile unread PR activity before excluding review candidates
review-073.detail: Only three event kinds seed review candidates. After an approval is acknowledged, an external push can stale it and produce an unread `pr.ci_passed` event, but the digest never examines that PR. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-digest-repro.ts"` printed `Unread: [ "pr.ci_passed" ]`, an approval with `stale: true`, and `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 0; Blocked lands: 0`.
review-073.failure_scenario: A consumer acknowledges the original PR and approval events. Someone pushes another commit, invalidating approval; CI passes and adds a new feed event. The next session digest incorrectly reports no review work.

review-073.title: Exclude active corrective rounds from PRs awaiting review
review-073.detail: The review predicate checks approval and landing state but ignores `review.rounds`. Requesting changes invalidates approval immediately, so a PR is reported as awaiting review while the factory is still applying those changes. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-digest-repro.ts"` printed `Review round: queued` followed by `Needs you: 0; PRs awaiting review: 1; Blocked lands: 0`.
review-073.failure_scenario: The original PR event remains unread and a changes verdict creates a queued review round. A fresh session is prompted to review the old head before the corrective round delivers.

review-073.title: Handle closed PRs before historical landing blockers
review-073.detail: A blocked land entry takes precedence over a saved CLOSED PR observation. Status therefore recommends retrying landing even though `LandQueue.request` rejects closed PRs. Reproduction: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-status-repro.ts"` returned `"state":"Landing blocked"` and `"nextAction":"Inspect the land reason, resolve the blocker, then request limitless_land again."` for a CLOSED PR.
review-073.failure_scenario: Landing blocks on CI, then an operator closes the PR. The blocked entry remains historical state, and limitless_status directs the next agent to an operation the API refuses.

review-073.title: MCP review approvals are recorded as reviewer "human"
review-073.detail: The limitless_review input schema is strict and leaves out `reviewer`. The call passes `ReviewVerdictSchema.parse(input)` without one, and submitReview then falls back to `parsed.data.reviewer ?? "human"` (src/pipeline/review-round.ts:193). So an approval an AI agent submits over MCP is stored in review_approvals as reviewer "human". The review.approved feed trigger then shows it as "approved at <sha> by human". Other paths label their source: the CLI sends `reviewer: process.env.USER ?? "cli"`, and MCP's own answer tool sends `by: "mcp"`. This approval is what lets limitless_land merge, so the audit trail misattributes who approved a merge.
review-073.failure_scenario: An agent calls limitless_review({run, verdict:"approve", reviewedSha}). The review_approvals row has reviewer='human', and the feed item reads 'approved at abc123 by human'. The operator believes a person approved the merge.

review-073.title: Unrequested change to publication-gate semantics: nested encodings now block publication even with an empty denylist
review-073.detail: privateMatches now decodes repeatedly: percent-encoding plus a new `\\+u` Unicode-escape pass, for up to 5 rounds. If the text is still changing after that, it returns a synthetic entry 0, so checkPrivateText, checkPrivateRange and blob scans block publication even when private-strings.txt is empty. Before this change, an empty denylist never blocked. These functions gate every commit, patch and blob the factory publishes, and the request (MCP tools plus a digest) didn't ask to change them. The extra layers also add up to 6× the text to NFKC-normalize on large diffs.
review-073.failure_scenario: [redacted diagnostic]

review-073.title: Unreadable privacy policy hides create_run/land results after the mutation succeeded
review-073.detail: CallTool now replaces every tool's output except limitless_status with 'Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable.' when loadOutputPrivacy() returns null, for example when private-strings.txt is not valid UTF-8 or can't be read. The mutation has still run by then. create_run has queued a run and land has queued an entry, but the agent never receives the id. limitless_status in that state also returns neither the requested plain-language state nor the next action, only land id/state and a question count, even though both strings are generated constants.
review-073.failure_scenario: private-strings.txt contains invalid UTF-8. An agent calls limitless_create_run, a run is queued, and the agent only sees 'Tool output withheld'. It retries and creates a duplicate run.

review-073.title: All MCP tool outputs, including pre-existing tools, are now filtered by the private-strings publication denylist
review-073.detail: The CallTool handler now runs `privateOutputData(result, privacy)` on every tool result. It also replaces the whole result with `{message: "Tool output withheld; privacy policy unavailable."}` when private-strings.txt can't be read. This changes the existing create_run, get_run, list_runs, feed, answer and resolve tools, which the request never asked for. private-strings.txt is documented (docs/GUIDE.md) as a publication guard for audit, delivery and land, not as a filter on the local operator's own agent. Any string field that contains a listed value is replaced wholesale, as are object keys. A user who lists their private org or hostname (the documented use) loses repo names, prompts, PR U
review-073.failure_scenario: With LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR/private-strings.txt containing `acme`, `privateOutputData({repo:"acme/app", prompt:"fix acme login", acme:1}, privacy)` returns `{repo:"[withheld: private text]", prompt:"[withheld: private text]", "[withheld: private text]":1}`. I verified this with a probe script. limitle

review-073.title: Unrequested change to the publication gate's private-string matching
review-073.detail: privateMatches now also decodes `\uXXXX` escapes and repeats decoding up to 5 layers. If decoding hasn't converged by then, it returns a sentinel `{entry: 0}` match even when the denylist is empty. That makes audit (gates/audit.ts) and repo scanning (git/repos.ts) block publication with "exceeds the private text decoding limit". This changes gate semantics for every run, well outside the MCP/digest task and its ~200-line budget, and the GUIDE docs weren't updated.
review-073.failure_scenario: [redacted diagnostic]

review-073.title: limitless_status drops state and nextAction when the privacy policy is unreadable
review-073.detail: When `privacy` is null, `result()` returns only `{land:{id,state}, openQuestions}`. It omits the plain-language state and next action, which are the tool's whole purpose under the request. Most of those are fixed strings generated by the code itself.
review-073.failure_scenario: private-strings.txt exists but isn't valid UTF-8 or can't be read, so limitless_status returns `{land:null, openQuestions:0}` with no state or next action.

review-073.title: Digest caps the line count but not line length
review-073.detail: Each row embeds the full quoted title and summary, and for questions the full question text. Land-blocked reasons and question bodies can be long, so the "at most 20 lines" SessionStart output can still inject a large block into every new session's context.
review-073.failure_scenario: A land.blocked item whose reason holds a multi-kilobyte CI excerpt prints one very long digest line at every session start.

review-076.title: Recheck current origin eligibility before dispatching queued calls
review-076.detail: The exclusion check runs when constructing a target. Concierge retains that target across provider-slot waits and ignores catalog invalidation, so a subsequent catalog edit can mark the model excluded without preventing dispatch. Evals likewise retain targets across preparation and admission waits. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/origin-review.test.ts" -t 'already queued'` reproducibly failed: `Calls after exclusion: [{"modelId":"fake/m","currentExclusion":"origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)"}]`; the assertion expected no calls.
review-076.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"], occupy a provider's sole slot, and enqueue chat using a runtime model recorded as US/US. PATCH its origin and baseOrigin to CN while chat waits, then release the slot. Fresh routing rejects the model, but the queued chat still sends its context to it.

review-076.title: Preserve the exclusion reason when chat has no candidate
review-076.detail: Concierge discards RouteDecision.skipped and reports a generic capacity error when exclusions eliminate every candidate. The requested failure reason therefore reaches pipeline invocations but not chat. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun test "$TMPDIR/origin-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected to contain: "origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)"; Received: "No model available for chat"`.
review-076.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] and a chat policy containing only a CN-origin model, then submit a chat message. The response hides the safety constraint behind a generic capacity error.

review-076.title: Preserve the exclusion reason when chat has no eligible model
review-076.detail: Concierge.interpret discards RouteDecision.skipped and consumes only candidates. When the new origin filter removes the remaining chat candidates, it exits with "No model available for chat" (or a previous generic model failure), omitting the required "origin excluded (<origin>; baseOrigin=<baseOrigin>)" reason. The new diagnostic handling in RunContext.invoke does not cover this separate invocation path.
review-076.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"], exhaust the allowed providers in the chat policy, and submit a chat message while the remaining fallback has origin/baseOrigin CN. No excluded model is called, but the returned error omits the exclusion reason.

review-076.title: Filter excluded verifiers before selecting a panel target
review-076.detail: The exclusion check runs after the production panel selects one verifier. In src/pipeline/engine.ts:1336–1342, every configured verifier enters pickVerifier, and the chosen target is offered alone through `only`. An excluded first verifier therefore causes NoCapacityError even when a later allowed verifier is available. A focused Bun probe using the existing pickVerifier function and real Router returned `selected: openrouter/deepseek-v4-pro`, an empty selectedRoute with `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)`, and a nonempty allowedRoute for codex/sol.
review-076.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] and a production panel with verifier.targets=["openrouter/deepseek-v4-pro","codex/sol"]. An Anthropic finder raises a finding, and Codex is available. The panel picks DeepSeek, routing rejects it, and verification fails instead of selecting Codex.

review-076.title: Filter excluded verifiers before selecting from a panel list
review-076.detail: The engine resolves every listed verifier and passes them to pickVerifier without filtering origins. pickVerifier can select an excluded model, after which the router receives an `only` constraint and rejects it. The panel fails even when another listed, independent verifier is allowed and available.
review-076.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] and a panel verifier list with a CN model first and an allowed US model second. Neither verifier raised the finding and both have independent vendors. pickVerifier chooses the CN model; routing rejects it without considering the US verifier.

review-076.title: Preserve origin exclusion reasons when chat routing exhausts candidates
review-076.detail: The concierge discards RouteDecision.skipped and uses only candidates. When exclusions leave no chat candidate, it throws `No model available for chat`, or an earlier generic model failure, without the required origin exclusion reason. The new diagnostic handling in RunContext does not cover this invocation path.
review-076.failure_scenario: Configure exclude_origins=["CN"] with a chat policy whose allowed providers are exhausted and whose remaining model is CN-origin. The router correctly excludes it, but the chat invocation fails with a generic message that omits `origin excluded (CN; baseOrigin=CN)`.

review-076.title: Recheck origin eligibility after waiting for chat capacity
review-076.detail: Chat retains its selected ModelTarget across acquire and preflight without checking router.policyRevision or current catalog eligibility. review-100.detail:
The affected-reference filter uses the current catalog, so it discards every reference to a model being added. An addition can therefore persist a model incompatible with an existing stored routing reference. review-100.failure_scenario: SQLite retains triage.default = ["codex/restored@high"] while that model is absent. An operator adds codex/restored supporting only "none". The API accepts and persists it; the next daemon startup throws while restoring routing.

review-100.title: IPv6 remote hosts abort local management before SSH
review-100.detail: An IPv6 address is a valid SSH destination, but interpolating it without URL brackets throws before any remote command runs. This also prevents down from stopping the service, even though down needs no health probe. Exact command: bun -e 'import { manageLocal } from "./src/cli/local.ts"; console.log(await manageLocal("down", {remoteHost:"::1", command:async()=>({stdout:"",stderr:"",exitCode:0}), probe:async()=>true}));' Output: TypeError: Invalid URL; input: "http://::1:8080"; code: "ERR_INVALID_URL" at src/cli/local.ts:93.
review-100.failure_scenario: [local].remote_host contains an unbracketed IPv6 address, with a configured provider using a valid bracketed IPv6 base URL. All local actions throw before reaching SSH.

review-100.title: Legacy evals referencing removed targets still cannot resume
review-100.detail: The new compatibility test expects HTTP 400 on resume, contradicting the requirement that pre-change records still resume. EvalRunner.resume passes the unchanged stored request to submit, whose validateRequest rejects unknown model ids; stored switch chains are also strictly resolved before submission. Consequently, one removed target prevents the entire eval from resuming, even when other configured targets remain available.
review-100.failure_scenario: An interrupted eval created before the catalog removal has a stored request containing the removed model id and a live model id. POST /api/evals/:id/resume returns 400 with 'unknown model ID', so the live model's unfinished trials cannot continue.

review-100.title: Old [local] config keys are ignored without a warning
review-100.detail: main.ts now reads only `remote_host`, `remote_model_path` and `remote_llama_binary`. An existing config.toml that still uses the old machine-prefixed keys loses remote llama.cpp management with no message. `local up` / `status` just report oMLX, as if remote management were not configured. The warning can be generic and doesn't need to name the old keys, e.g. warn about any unrecognised `[local]` key.

review-100.title: Invalid remote_host crashes `local` with a raw URL TypeError
review-100.detail: `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` throws on a host the URL parser rejects, such as a value with a space or an IPv6 address without brackets. The command dies with an unexplained TypeError before reporting anything, oMLX included. An `ssh` destination that starts with `-` is also passed through as an ssh option. The config file is owner-controlled, so this is a robustness problem, not a security one.

review-100.title: Retry and eval resume of records naming the removed id are refused, not resumed
review-100.detail: The new test asserts that resuming an interrupted eval whose request names the retired model returns 400 "unknown model ID". `retryRun` similarly re-validates an inherited `run.models` chain strictly, so retrying a failed run pinned to the old id also throws. Live runs routing through chains with the old id work, and so does rendering. But the request says records written before the change should 'still render and resume'. For evals and retries, the old ids now require operator action instead of skipping the retired target as the router does.

review-100.title: Scope larger than budget; catalog-edit validation semantics changed
review-100.detail:
The source diff adds about 194 lines and removes 94, against a budget of about 120 changed lines (mostly deletions). It also changes behaviour beyond the rename:
- `remove()` no longer has its explicit operator-policy guard; `apply` enforces it instead, with a different error message.
- Terminal runs no longer block model deletion.
- Catalog POSTs now succeed despite references that were already invalid.
- Setup.tsx gains UI for unavailable references.

These changes support requirement 4, but the scoped re-validation in `apply` is hard to follow.

review-100.title: Runtime models with a missing provider are now loaded, and the strict validators still accept them in new writes
review-100.detail: Factory used to throw `unknown provider` for a runtime model whose provider was not defined. It now logs a warning and adds the model to `this.models`. validatePolicy and validateRunModels (`src/router/policy.ts:43-60`) only resolve the model id; for an undefined provider, `transportError` returns null. So once such a model is loaded, a new operator routing write or a new run pin naming it passes validation even though it can never route. The comment in `retired.ts` says "new writes still go through the strict validators", but those validators do not check that the provider exists.

review-100.title: Unrequested behaviour change: catalog removal now ignores finished runs, and the test protecting the old invariant was rewritten
review-100.detail: `apply()` now skips terminal runs when a model is removed, and `remove()` no longer refuses up front when operator policy references the model. The earlier test "catalog validates stored chains ... regardless of status" was rewritten to cover only live statuses, plus a new test that removal succeeds for finished runs. The scoped `affected()` validation was already enough to stop old runs that name the retired id from blocking catalog edits, so skipping terminal runs is extra policy. Together with the Setup.tsx diagnostics and credential redaction, source changes come to roughly 280 lines against the ~120-line budget.
review-100.failure_scenario: An operator deletes a runtime model that a succeeded run pinned. Before this change the delete was refused; now it succeeds. The run still renders because unknown ids are handled generically, but no reviewer asked for this change of invariant.

review-100.title: Matching the remote host to a provider only works for a base URL of exactly http://<remote_host>:8080
review-100.detail: `up` and `down` change enablement only for a provider whose `openaiBaseUrl` origin equals `http://${remote_host}:8080`. Some setups won't match: an SSH alias that differs from the URL host, a `user@host` destination, an SSH-forwarded `127.0.0.1:18080` endpoint, or a different port. In those cases enablement is silently never toggled, and the health probe uses an unauthenticated fallback URL. OPERATIONS.md documents the matching rule, so this is a usability gap rather than a bug.
review-100.failure_scenario: Set `remote_host = "gpu"` (an alias in ~/.ssh/config) while the provider's `base_url` is `http://10.0.0.5:8080/v1`. `limitless local up` starts the unit but reports the endpoint as unreachable (the probe hits http://gpu:8080 without a key) and never enables the provider.

review-100.title: `limitless local` crashes on an IPv6 or host:port remote_host
review-100.detail: `manageLocal` now runs `new URL(`http://${host}:8080`)` to find the matching provider. review-100.title: Persisted routing cells naming removed models are now silently dropped, and the test that guarded the old behavior was deleted
review-100.detail: Before this change, startup threw if a persisted operator cell named an explicitly removed model (e.g. `claude/fable`, which has an owner-decision entry in REMOVED_MODELS). The error carried that owner-decision reason. Startup also threw a helpful 'is a model ID, not a provider' error for a model id stored in `prefer`. Now `filterRetiredTargets` and the `retiredReason` prefer filter quietly drop both cases with a generic 'retired reference: X is not in the catalog' warning. The old test (`startup validates persisted operator cells and preferences against today's catalog`) was replaced by one that only checks an invalid effort.

review-100.title: Scope is well over budget and changes catalog-removal rules beyond the request
review-100.detail:
About 280 lines of source changed against a budget of about 120. The extras:
- a new `unavailable` diagnostics field in the routing and catalog snapshots, with credential-redaction plumbing
- new UI in `ui/pages/Setup.tsx`
- the `remove()` check that blocked removing a runtime model referenced by operator cells was deleted; the scoped operator-layer validation now covers that
- a new rule lets a runtime model be removed even when finished runs reference it

The scoping itself is needed so that runs and cells naming retired ids don't block every catalog edit. The rule change for finished runs and the UI diagnostics were not requested.

Stored routing cells and preferences are now filtered generically, but retryRun passes the inherited run.models through createRun -> validateRunModels. That validator still rejects unknown model ids, so a run that pinned the machine-named model (or any removed id) cannot be retried. The retryRun comment already says inherited chains 'predate this constraint', and they could be filtered with filterRetiredTargets the same way persisted operator cells are.

review-106.detail: The deploy CLI never loads configuration or otherwise registers provider credentials. A fresh `bun -` probe invoking deploy with the existing deploy-test setup, OPENROUTER_API_KEY=`synthetic-review-deploy-provider-secret`, and an injected failing test command printed `registeredCredentials=0`, followed by `Error: Command failed (1): bun test\nerror: synthetic-review-deploy-provider-secret\n(fail) assertion`; the stdout tail also contained the same value. Tracing src/cli/main.ts's deploy branch confirms there is no
review-106.failure_scenario: Run `limitless deploy` in a fresh process with a configured provider credential. A failing gate echoes that credential, and the deploy error exposes it unchanged.

review-106.title: Bound the carry when credential matches overlap repeatedly
review-106.detail: The loop can retreat cut all the way to zero on every chunk. For a registered credential `aaaaaaaa` and an all-`a` stream, each crossing match moves cut backward seven characters until the entire stream remains in pending. tailLimit only bounds emitted text, so it does not bound this buffer. A `bun -` probe using the proc tests' PassThrough/spawn-fixture approach, 400 writes of 10,000 `a` characters, redactOutput=true and tailLimit=100 showed per-write time increasing from 1.13 ms to 12.42 ms and heap usage increasing from about 2 MB to 29 MB; the returned tail was only 100 characters. Continuing output grows retained memory without bound and repeatedly rescans the accumulated stream.
review-106.failure_scenario: A registered credential is a repetitive value such as `aaaaaaaa`, and a gate prints a long repetitive stream. The daemon retains the full raw stream and performs increasing work per chunk despite its configured tail limit.

review-106.title: Deploy gate redaction does nothing in production: the deploy CLI process never registers credentials
review-106.detail: The `deploy` case in src/cli/main.ts imports ./service.ts and calls svc.deploy without calling loadConfig(). registerCredential is called only from src/config.ts:182 (inside loadConfig), and neither service.ts nor its imports load config. So in a real `limitless deploy` process the credential set is empty, and both `redactOutput: true` and `redactGateStreams` return the text unchanged. The deploy error still contains any provider API key a check prints. The new deploy tests call registerCredential themselves in the test process, which hides the gap.
review-106.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless deploy --smoke`. A test in the release checkout fails and prints the provider API key from the environment or a fixture. registeredCredentials() is empty in that CLI process, so the thrown deploy error and the console show the key unredacted.

review-106.title: About 4.7x over the line budget, and redaction is spread across many places instead of the single point requested

The budget is about 30 net source lines. The diff adds 140 net source lines and also redacts in: every HTTP JSON response and SSE message (`serialize`), the artifact endpoint (re-parsing and re-serializing every artifact), RunContext state on load, checkpoint reads, implementPrompt, reviewPrompt, verifyPrompt, formatGateFeedback, renderReport and formatGateOutput. It also adds JSON-escaped credential variants, per-stream truncation flags and a change to the MCP privacy policy. AGENTS.md says to stay within the issue's line budget and t

review-106.detail: `text.includes("[redacted]")` now replaces the whole string with "[withheld: private text]". review-050.detail: Recovery only examines ctx.state.worktreePath. During preparation, createWorktree creates the checkout before that path is persisted. review-050.detail: The new test parks the run in phase 'loop' with no needsHumanReason. It doesn't cover resuming at delivery or with needsHumanReason set, which is where the gap above is. The worktree still has no `.git-paths` record, so every git call in `trustedEnv` throws "Missing trusted Git paths" and the draft PR is never opened. review-058.detail: Catalog history comes exclusively from the component-local session signal, populated by this component's mutation callbacks. review-058.title: Out-of-scope Playwright dependency plus a postinstall script that downloads Chromium
review-058.detail: The change adds `playwright` as a devDependency (the flagged bun.lock change). review-088.title: Dirty check on a fresh index re-hashes every file, so files that rely on a global filter (such as git-lfs) would show as modified
review-088.detail: read-tree fills the private index with no stat data, so status re-hashes every tracked file. safe_git disables all filter.* keys, including global ones like filter.lfs.clean. A smudged LFS file in the work tree would therefore hash differently from its pointer blob and be reported as modified, which refuses the land. Before this change, the clone's index kept stat data and avoided the re-hash. This repository has no .gitattributes, so nothing breaks today. The request did ask for these same hardening flags.

review-088.title: Writing info/exclude assumes `git init` created info/ from templates
review-088.detail: `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` needs the info/ directory. That directory comes only from the init template; objects/info is always created, but info/ is not. If a user's global config sets `init.templateDir` to a directory without info/, or a packaged git has no template dir, the redirect fails and `set -e` stops every land with a raw bash error.
review-088.failure_scenario: Reproduced: `git -c init.templateDir=<empty dir> init --bare r` produces only HEAD, config, objects/{info,pack} and refs. The printf to r/info/exclude would then fail with 'No such file or directory'.

The `checks:pager` scenario plants core.pager and pager.status but runs without a TTY, and git never starts a pager without one. So the scenario passes even if both `--no-pager` and the isolation are removed. Only the separate assertion that post-check calls use the private git dir would catch a regression.
review-088.failure_scenario: Remove `--no-pager` from safe_git and keep isolation: checks:pager still passes, so the test does not cover the pager part.

review-088.title: Writing info/exclude fails when the global init.templateDir has no info/ directory
review-088.detail: `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That only happens when the template dir has one. With a global `init.templateDir` pointing at a hooks-only template (e.g. the git-secrets setup), `init --bare` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs (verified: `git -c init.templateDir=$TMPDIR/empty init --bare tdt` gives no info/). The redirect fails, and under `set -e` the script exits with a raw shell 'No such file or directory' instead of a generic refusal. It fails safe, but no land can succeed for that user. The request asked for a pseudo-terminal or, failing that, an assertion that `GIT_PAGER` or `--no-pager` is used. review-088.detail: The line `printf '%s' "$exclude" > "$push_repo/info/exclude"` assumes `git init --bare` created `info/`. That directory comes from the init template. With an empty template (for example a global `init.templateDir` pointing at an empty directory, or `--template=`), `info/` does not exist. I confirmed that `git init --bare --template=` creates only HEAD, config, objects and refs. review-088.title: Fresh index without stat data makes smudged LFS files look modified
review-088.detail: After `read-tree`, the private index has no stat data, so `status` hashes every work-tree file. `safe_git` blanks every `filter.*` key, including the global `filter.lfs.*` ones, so files that LFS smudged on checkout hash to their real contents, not their pointer blobs. They therefore show as modified and the land is refused. The old in-clone status used an index with cached stat data and would not have hashed them. This repository has no tracked `.gitattributes` or LFS files today, so there is no current impact.

review-105.title: MCP/digest privacy filter now withholds any text containing the literal "[redacted]"
review-105.detail: loadOutputPrivacy now returns "[withheld: private text]" for any string that contains "[redacted]". It used to pass already-redacted text through. This affects every MCP tool result (through privateOutputData) and every digest line or error. Any field that legitimately contains the redaction marker loses its whole content, and so does user-written text that contains the literal. Examples are run errors, gate output, and agent tool results already redacted by the harnesses. No test covers the change, and the request does not ask for it.
review-105.failure_scenario: I checked this with a script: `loadOutputPrivacy()("Check test failed: error: credential [redacted]\n(fail) assertion foo.test.ts")` returns `[withheld: private text]`. Before the change it returned the text unchanged. So an MCP status query for a run whose gate output had a credential redacted lose

review-105.title: reviewPrompt VT-strips the inline patch, so reviewers cannot see escape sequences that an external PR introduces
review-105.detail: `input = redactGateData(input)` runs stripVTControlCharacters over every string in the review input. That includes `patch`, which is inlined for PR verification of external, untrusted changes. Raw ESC/CSI sequences added by the change, such as terminal-injection or concealment codes in source files, are silently removed from what the reviewer sees. The verify prompt and the artifact endpoint do the same.
review-105.failure_scenario: An external PR adds `\x1b[8m` (conceal) or cursor-movement sequences to a source file. The patch shown inline in the review prompt has them stripped, so the reviewer has no evidence to flag them.

review-105.title: confinementError is now always written and output is VT-stripped, which changes how an older release reads new results
review-105.detail: The removed comment said confinementError was 'present only when set … so results stay readable by … older releases'. It is now always written, and `output` is now VT-stripped. An older release reads `!!confinementError || output.includes(marker)`. For output whose raw text was `Oper\x1b[0mation`, the new version records confinementError: false. After stripping, the stored output contains the full marker, so an older release reading the row would classify it as a confinement error. This only matters on rollback.
review-105.failure_scenario: New code stores {confinementError:false, output:"sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted"} from a check that printed an ANSI-interrupted marker. After a rollback, the older release marks the check as a confinement error.

review-087.title: Clean-filter tests never hit the key-enumeration race from #402
review-087.detail: Both clean-filter scenarios plant filter.attack.clean before safe_git's `git config --name-only --get-regexp` read: one during `bun run check`, the other in the fake `gh pr view`. A clone-level safe_git call would therefore always neutralise the filter through --config-env, so the marker could never run even if the dirty check went back to the clone's config. In my mutation run, a clone-level `safe_git status --porcelain` passed the marker assertion in these tests; they failed only on the argv assertions for the status call.
review-087.failure_scenario: Mutate land-pr.sh to run `safe_git status --porcelain` against the clone before the isolated check. checks:clean-filter and pre-push:clean-filter still pass `expect(existsSync(marker)).toBe(false)` and fail only because the status argv check expects --untracked-files=normal.

review-087.title: An in-progress rebase is not refused
review-087.detail: The state check covers MERGE_HEAD, CHERRY_PICK_HEAD and REVERT_HEAD (exactly the request) but not rebase-merge/ or rebase-apply/. A half-finished rebase with a clean tree would land its detached HEAD. The pinned-SHA comparison still guarantees that what's pushed is what was checked.
review-087.failure_scenario: The orchestrator leaves a rebase stopped mid-way with a clean tree; land-pr pushes the partially rebased HEAD.

review-096.title: Redundant runtime claude/haiku-5.5 row can never be removed; warning repeats forever
review-096.detail: Startup skips the stored runtime model (continue) and keeps only the built-in in this.models. RuntimeCatalog.remove(id) calls editable(id), which finds the built-in (source undefined/'code') and throws '<id>: code and config models are read-only'. So `limitless catalog remove claude/haiku-5.5` cannot delete the stale runtime_models row; it persists indefinitely, the daemon warns on every start, and the warning gives no remediation. The request's alternative path (document `limitless catalog remove`) is therefore also not workable.
review-096.failure_scenario: Installation with an existing runtime entry claude/haiku-5.5 (as stated in the request) upgrades; daemon logs the redundant warning; operator runs `limitless catalog remove claude/haiku-5.5` -> error 'claude/haiku-5.5: code and config models are read-only'; row remains and warning recurs every start

review-096.title: Collision handling is hard-coded to the literal id claude/haiku-5.5
review-096.detail: The request describes the general case of a runtime entry that has the same id as a new built-in. The implementation special-cases the string 'claude/haiku-5.5'. The next built-in that shadows an existing runtime entry will stop daemon startup with 'catalog collision', which is the failure the request asked to prevent.
review-096.failure_scenario: A future release adds a built-in codex/foo while an installation already has a runtime codex/foo -> Factory constructor throws 'catalog collision: codex/foo' and the daemon fails to start.

review-096.title: Pin test now hard-codes the decision date and eval ids
review-096.detail: The test previously read `decided` from overrides.json. It now asserts the literal '2026-10-07' and two eval ids, so every future owner decision needs a test edit even when the pin works correctly.
review-096.failure_scenario: The next triage owner decision updates overrides.json; this test fails although the pin behaves correctly.

review-096.title: Redundant runtime claude/haiku-5.5 entry can no longer be removed, so the startup warning is permanent
review-096.detail: The Factory skips the stored runtime row and keeps the built-in model (no `source`, so it counts as "code") in `this.models`. `limitless catalog remove claude/haiku-5.5` calls `RuntimeCatalog.remove`, which goes through `editable()` (src/router/runtime-catalog.ts). That looks up `this.models`, finds the built-in, and throws "claude/haiku-5.5: code and config models are read-only". The `runtime_models` row therefore stays in the DB forever, and every daemon start prints the redundancy warning. Neither the warning nor EVIDENCE.md gives the operator a way to clear it. The request asked to log that the entry is redundant (or document `catalog remove`), and here the redundant entry can't be remov
