The operator runs `limitless catalog remove claude/haiku-5.5` and gets 'code and config models are read-only'. The row and the warning persist on every restart.

review-096.title: Collision tolerance is hardcoded to one model id
review-096.detail: The fallback that prefers the built-in applies only when `existing.id === "claude/haiku-5.5"`. The underlying problem — an operator adds a model at runtime and a later release ships it as a built-in — is generic. The next built-in that collides with a runtime entry will make startup throw 'catalog collision' again, which is the failure step 4 asked to prevent. A literal model id inside Factory construction is also inconsistent with the rest of the catalog code, which is data-driven.
review-096.failure_scenario: An operator runs `limitless catalog add claude/foo`, and a later release adds a built-in `claude/foo`. Daemon startup throws 'catalog collision: claude/foo'.

review-096.title: Redundant runtime claude/haiku-5.5 row can never be removed, so the warning repeats on every startup
review-096.detail: At startup the colliding runtime model is skipped (`continue`), and only the built-in ends up in this.models. RuntimeCatalog.remove() calls editable(id), which looks the id up in this.models, finds the built-in (no source, so 'code') and throws `claude/haiku-5.5: code and config models are read-only`. The persisted runtime_models row therefore stays forever. The operator gets '[catalog] claude/haiku-5.5: redundant runtime entry' on every boot with no way to act on it. The catalog snapshot and API don't show the shadowed row either. The request offered two options: log that the entry is redundant, or document `limitless catalog remove`. The second implies removal should work, yet this change
review-096.failure_scenario: An installation has a runtime claude/haiku-5.5 row from `limitless catalog add`. After upgrading, every daemon start logs the redundant-entry warning. Running `limitless catalog remove claude/haiku-5.5` returns the error 'claude/haiku-5.5: code and config models are read-only', and the row and warni

review-096.title: Collision handling hardcodes the single id 'claude/haiku-5.5' instead of a general rule
review-096.detail: The startup loop special-cases `existing.id === "claude/haiku-5.5"`. Any other runtime entry that later duplicates a newly added built-in still throws `catalog collision` and crashes the daemon at startup. That is exactly the failure this step was meant to prevent, and it will recur with the next built-in model. A model id hardcoded in Factory wiring is also out of keeping with the rest of the catalog code.
review-096.failure_scenario: A future release adds a built-in `claude/foo`, and an installation already has a runtime `claude/foo`. Factory throws `catalog collision: claude/foo` and the daemon fails to start.

review-096.title: Frozen identity test now hides Haiku 5.5 joining widened chains in every role
review-096.detail: existingSnapshot() strips claude/haiku-5.5 from candidates and skipped lists for all roles and constraints. Running identitySnapshot() shows Haiku 5.5 as a widened candidate in summarize, chat, spec, plan, implement, review and verify whenever a minTier constraint applies. For example, implement.small with {minTier:1} now ends in `...claude/haiku, claude/haiku-5.5@medium`, and chat with free_first/minTier 3 gives `claude/haiku, claude/haiku-5.5@medium`. As a runtime entry, the model was kept out of widening (see 'runtime models stay out of escalation and free widening'). As a built-in it now joins widening everywhere. The comment says this is 'covered above', but the new tests cover only tri
review-096.failure_scenario: An escalation or constraint with minTier ≤ 3 on summarize, chat or implement can now place claude/haiku-5.5 in the candidate list. The modified frozen test would not detect it, nor any later reordering involving Haiku 5.5 in those roles.

review-096.title: Startup can still fail when operator routing names an effort the built-in doesn't support
review-096.detail: After the built-in replaces the runtime entry, RuntimePolicy's constructor validates stored operator routing cells against the built-in's supportedEfforts (low/medium/high). If the runtime entry declared other efforts (e.g. none or xhigh), and an operator cell or pinned run uses them, validatePolicy throws and Factory construction fails. I confirmed that validatePolicy rejects `claude/haiku-5.5@xhigh` and `@none` with 'Unsupported effort ... supported: low, medium, high'. This contradicts the requirement that startup must not fail.
review-096.failure_scenario: The runtime entry had efforts [none, low, medium, high], and an operator set `triage.small` to `claude/haiku-5.5@none` with `limitless routing set`. After upgrade, `new Factory()` throws `triage.small: ... Unsupported effort "none" for claude/haiku-5.5` and the daemon will not start.

review-096.title: triage.default reason drops earlier decision history instead of appending to it
review-096.detail: The previous reason recorded why Luna/Codex leads and OpenRouter Luna follows (eval-mump7s7re29l), and that Sonnet 5.5 replaced Sonnet 5 as the last fallback on 2026-10-04. The new text replaces all of that. Other entries such as implement.* and review.large append each later owner decision to the earlier rationale. The pin message printed by `limitless eval policy` no longer explains the rest of the chain.
review-096.failure_scenario: An operator who runs `limitless eval policy` sees the triage pin reason with no explanation for why codex/luna@low/none, OpenRouter Luna and Sonnet 5.5 are in the chain.

review-040.title: Apply new configuration to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Init writes missing provider and merge settings but skips service installation whenever the original daemon check passed. The daemon loads configuration at startup and has no reload path, so init reports success while it continues using the old settings. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` failed with `Expected to contain: "install"; Received: ["write /fake/config/config.toml", "write /fake/home/smoke-last.json"]`.
review-040.failure_scenario: Run init against a healthy daemon with a partial config, adding a detected local provider or filling the missing merge policy. The written settings remain inactive until a separate restart.

review-040.title: Smoke-test the effective configured providers
review-040.detail: The production smoke adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts, which selects providers, endpoints and models from the static catalog. Newly detected local providers are never exercised, and configured endpoint overrides are ignored. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/smoke-review.test.ts"` used fake harnesses and a zero execution budget to inspect scheduled checks; it listed only built-in provider rows and failed `Expected: true; Received: false` for inclusion of configured local-1234.
review-040.failure_scenario: Init adds local-1234 from its model listing, but its inference endpoint is broken. Smoke checks never call that provider, so setup can report success without validating it.

review-040.title: Check access to newly selected repositories before writing
review-040.detail: Doctor runs before repository selection and only reads repositories already in the original config. Fresh --repo arguments receive syntax validation but no access or SSO check before configuration is written. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed `GitHub commands: [["gh","auth","status"]]` and failed the assertion that `gh api repos/restricted/private` was called.
review-040.failure_scenario: On an empty config, run init --yes --repo restricted/private with an authenticated GitHub account lacking access or organization SSO authorization. Init writes the repository and proceeds without detecting the failure.

review-040.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
review-040.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with a hardcoded skipped message. Init never asks for or persists the requested choice. Reproduction: `bun test "$TMPDIR/setup-review.test.ts"` printed questions for repositories, merge policy and MCP only, then failed the discreet-question assertion with `Expected: true; Received: false`.
review-040.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init expecting to select discreet mode, or an agent uses --yes expecting its default to be configured. Neither path configures it.

review-040.title: Apply changed config to an already-running daemon
review-040.detail: The service step only checks the preflight daemon status. If init writes new providers or a merge policy while the daemon is healthy, it skips installation/restart. Factory loads these settings at startup, so setup reports success while the daemon retains its old configuration. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" reload` printed providers.added=[claude,codex,local-1234], effects=[smoke,mcp], then failed: `AssertionError: new provider config must reach the already-running daemon`.
review-040.failure_scenario: A healthy daemon is running when init detects a new local provider or adds github.merge="pr". Config is written, but subsequent runs still use the previous catalog or merge default.

review-040.title: Check requested repository access before writing config
review-040.detail: Doctor runs before repositories supplied through --repo or prompts are considered, and only reads a repository already in config. Fresh setup therefore never verifies access or organization SSO for its requested repository. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" repo`, with a fake repository API returning an SSO 403, printed `{"code":0,"ghReads":[],"effects":["smoke","mcp"]}` and failed: `AssertionError: init must reject a requested repository with denied SSO access`.
review-040.failure_scenario: On an empty config, run init --yes --repo private-org/denied with gh authenticated but lacking organization SSO authorization. Setup writes config and proceeds without detecting the access failure.

review-040.title: Run smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
review-040.detail: The production smoke adapter calls the existing smoke main, which uses hard-coded PROVIDERS/MODELS rather than the config catalog. Newly detected local providers and custom endpoints are never exercised; both native CLIs are always exercised even when doctor permits one to be missing. Command `TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review.ts" smoke` enumerated checks with a zero budget and no network. It reported detected=[claude,codex,local-1234], but smoke names contained only built-in providers, then failed: `AssertionError: smoke must exercise the detected local provider`.
review-040.failure_scenario: Init detects a server on port 1234 and saves local-1234, but smoke never invokes it. Alternatively, a machine with only Claude passes preflight with a Codex warning and then fails smoke by invoking the absent Codex CLI.

review-040.title: Apply newly written settings to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Service installation is skipped whenever the preflight daemon check passes, even after init changes config.toml. The daemon retains its startup Config and provider catalog, so newly detected providers and the selected merge policy remain inactive. The probe returned `{"probe":"healthy daemon and new repo","code":0,"installs":0,"repoReads":[],"providersAdded":["claude","codex"],"merge":"pr"}`. In particular, a daemon started with the default auto merge policy can continue auto-merging after init reports the safer pr policy.
review-040.failure_scenario: Start a daemon with an empty config, then run init while its SHA matches. Init writes providers and github.merge="pr", reports success, and leaves the running daemon using its old settings.

review-040.title: Check access to repositories supplied during init
review-040.detail: Doctor runs before init collects repositories and only reads the first repository already in the saved config. Newly supplied --repo values or interactive answers are never checked for access or SSO before being persisted. The probe supplied private-org/blocked and returned code 0 with `"repoReads":[]`; its fake would record every gh API call. Thus the advertised repository preflight cannot diagnose organization access on a fresh installation.
review-040.failure_scenario: On an empty config, gh auth status succeeds but the token lacks access to the organization supplied through --repo. Init writes that repository and proceeds without detecting the access failure.

review-040.title: Run smoke checks against the configured provider catalog
review-040.detail: The new adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts main(), which still builds checks from hard-coded PROVIDERS and MODELS. It ignores detected local providers and configured endpoint/model overrides, and always checks both native CLIs. The probe configured ["claude","codex","local-1234"], but smoke enumeration contained only Claude, Codex, omlx, twilight, OpenRouter and TypeSafe checks, with none for local-1234. This leaves the newly configured backend unverified and can fail setup for a CLI that doctor explicitly allowed to be absent.
review-040.failure_scenario: Init detects a local server on port 1234 whose model listing succeeds but inference is broken. Its smoke phase never invokes that server, so setup can report success without validating the selected backend.

review-040.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
review-040.detail: Discreet mode is represented only by a hard-coded skipped message. Init neither asks for the preference nor persists it, despite this being an explicit setup requirement. The interactive probe recorded only provider, repository, merge-policy and MCP questions; no discreet-mode question occurred.
review-040.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init intending to enable discreet mode for work repositories. Setup completes without offering or saving that choice.

review-040.title: Apply configuration changes to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Init writes configuration but skips service installation whenever the daemon has the installed SHA. Factory retains its startup Config and has no configuration reload here, so new providers and the selected merge policy remain inactive. Command `bun /private/tmp/lr-zonOle/claude-501/setup-review.ts` ran setupCommand with mocked dependencies and returned `{"exit":0,"writtenConfig":true,"repositoryAccessChecks":[],"serviceEffects":[],"merge":"pr"}`.
review-040.failure_scenario: Start the daemon with no github.merge setting, then run init and accept pr. Init reports pr, but the running daemon continues registering repositories with auto merge.

review-040.title: Check access to requested repositories before persisting setup
review-040.detail: Doctor runs before --repo values or prompted repositories are incorporated and reads only the existing configuration. Newly requested repositories receive only syntax validation, so missing repository access or organization SSO authorization cannot stop setup. The mocked command `bun /private/tmp/lr-zonOle/claude-501/setup-review.ts` returned `{"exit":0,"writtenConfig":true,"repositoryAccessChecks":[],"serviceEffects":[],"merge":"pr"}` for --repo private-org/app.
review-040.failure_scenario: An authenticated GitHub user without access to private-org/app runs init --yes --repo private-org/app on an empty config. Setup persists the repository without checking its access or SSO requirements.

review-040.title: Limit smoke checks to available setup providers
review-040.detail: Doctor deliberately treats one absent agent CLI as a warning and provider detection omits it, but d.smoke invokes scripts/smoke.ts main, which unconditionally schedules live Claude and Codex checks. A supported single-CLI installation therefore proceeds through configuration and service changes, then fails smoke checks for the absent CLI on every rerun.
review-040.failure_scenario: Claude is installed and logged in while Codex is absent. Doctor allows init to continue, but init subsequently attempts Codex live checks and exits unsuccessfully.

review-040.title: Apply config changes to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Init writes new providers and merge settings but skips service startup whenever the preflight daemon SHA matches. Factory loads its catalog and configuration at construction, so the running daemon continues using the previous settings. The isolated command `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` produced `healthy daemon config update: {"effects":["write","write"],"service":"already set","merge":"pr"}`, confirming configuration writes without a service update.
review-040.failure_scenario: A daemon is healthy at the installed SHA. Re-running init adds a local provider or fills the missing merge policy. Init reports success, but the daemon cannot route to that provider and continues registering repositories with the old merge policy.

review-040.title: Run smoke checks against the detected provider configuration
review-040.detail: The production smoke adapter invokes a runner that imports the fixed PROVIDERS/MODELS catalogs and always schedules both native CLIs. It does not use the configured catalog or detected CLI availability. Newly detected local providers receive no live smoke check, while an absent CLI that doctor explicitly permits as a warning is still exercised. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/setup-review.ts"` with a zero smoke budget, preventing live calls, confirmed selection of both Claude and Codex plus the fixed backend list.
review-040.failure_scenario: Only Claude is installed and logged in. Doctor permits setup, but smoke attempts Codex and fails. Alternatively, init enables local-1234, yet its completion API is never exercised before setup reports success.

review-040.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup question
review-040.detail: Discreet mode is unconditionally replaced with a 'not available yet (#37)' summary string. Init never asks the required question or persists a choice, including during interactive setup. The request does not exempt this step.
review-040.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init on an empty configuration and wants discreet mode. Setup never offers the choice and finishes without configuring it.

review-040.title: Apply new configuration to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Init writes newly detected providers and merge settings, but skips service installation whenever the preflight daemon SHA matches. Factory loads its configuration and provider catalog at startup and has no reload here, so the running daemon continues using the old settings. Focused command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` produced `active daemon: {"added":["claude","codex","local-1234"],"merge":"pr","service":"already set","effects":["smoke","mcp"]}`.
review-040.failure_scenario: Run init against a healthy daemon with a partial config. Init adds a local provider and selects merge policy pr, but subsequent runs still use the daemon's previous provider catalog and merge policy.

review-040.title: Run smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
review-040.detail: The production adapter invokes the existing smoke main, which uses static PROVIDERS/MODELS and a hard-coded backend list. Newly detected or configured providers are never exercised. It also unconditionally exercises both native CLIs even though doctor permits one to be missing. A zero-budget check enumerated the actual smoke selection without making model or network calls: `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-smoke.ts"` output `{"configured":["claude","codex","local-1234"],"smokeProviders":["claude","codex","omlx","twilight","openrouter","typesafe"],"localChecks":[]}`.
review-040.failure_scenario: A newly detected local server lists models but cannot perform inference. Init's smoke checks never call it and can report success. Conversely, a machine with only Claude passes preflight but fails the unconditional Codex smoke checks after configuration has been written.

review-040.title: Check configured providers that lack an explicit health URL
review-040.detail: Provider diagnosis only makes a health request when healthUrl exists. Supported presets such as OpenRouter have no healthUrl, so doctor reports only that their key is present and never checks whether the provider answers. Focused command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with an OpenRouter preset and invalid test token returned only `provider:openrouter:key` as ok; the recorded HTTP requests were exclusively `/api/health` and `/api/github/access`.
review-040.failure_scenario: Configure the OpenRouter preset with an unavailable endpoint or unusable credentials. Doctor reports the configured provider key as present without attempting any provider health check.

review-040.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
review-040.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with an unconditional 'not available yet' summary string. Init neither asks the required question nor persists a choice, including in noninteractive default handling. The focused setup reproduction recorded only local-provider, repository, merge-policy, and MCP questions, followed by `discreet: skipped: discreet mode: not available yet (#37)`.
review-040.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init to enable discreet operation. No discreet-mode question appears, and setup completes without recording that preference.

review-040.title: Apply changed configuration to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Service installation is skipped whenever the preflight daemon SHA matches, even when init subsequently writes configuration. The daemon loads configuration only at startup, so newly detected providers and the selected merge policy remain inactive. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` produced `"effects":["smoke","mcp"]` while writing new providers and `"merge":"pr"`; no service action occurred.
review-040.failure_scenario: A healthy daemon started with no github.merge setting uses the auto default. Init writes merge=pr but leaves that daemon running; newly registered repositories can still receive auto merge policy.

review-040.title: Run smoke checks against the effective configured providers
review-040.detail: The production adapter calls scripts/smoke.ts main, which uses the static PROVIDERS and MODELS catalogs rather than the configuration init just wrote. It always schedules both native CLIs and fixed legacy backends, and never schedules newly detected local providers. The offline command `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"`, using a zero smoke budget to avoid model calls, printed `"configuredLocalTested":false` and scheduled claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter, and typesafe checks.
review-040.failure_scenario: A machine with Claude installed and Codex absent passes preflight with a Codex warning, but init subsequently runs Codex smoke checks. A detected local-1234 provider is saved without receiving any live smoke check.

review-040.title: Check requested repository access before persisting setup
review-040.detail: Doctor runs before flags.repo or prompted repositories enter the configuration. Those repositories receive only syntax validation before being saved, so setup never checks their access or organization SSO authorization. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/review-setup.ts"` with private/no-access returned `"result":0,"repositoryReads":[]` and persisted that repository.
review-040.failure_scenario: On an empty configuration, gh auth status succeeds but the token lacks access or SSO authorization for the repository passed through --repo. Init saves it and continues instead of stopping without partial configuration.

review-040.title: Do not treat a preset alias as the native provider
review-040.detail: Candidate deduplication treats e.preset === id as evidence that the native provider is already configured, even when the entry has a different explicit id. Provider semantics allow an entry such as id="work-claude", preset="claude" with endpoint overrides. That entry does not represent the detected native claude provider, but init skips adding the requested native preset.
review-040.failure_scenario: Configuration contains a work-claude provider derived from the Claude preset and pointed at a compatible server. The native Claude CLI is logged in, but init does not add its claude preset because the aliased entry has preset="claude".

review-040.title: Implement the requested discreet-mode setup choice
review-040.detail: Init never asks about discreet mode or persists a choice. It unconditionally returns a string saying the feature is unavailable, and the new test explicitly expects that omission. The original request includes discreet mode among the setup questions and does not exclude it from scope.
review-040.failure_scenario: A user runs interactive init to enable a repository in discreet mode. There is no prompt or configuration path for selecting it, and --yes likewise cannot persist its default.

review-040.title: Apply changed configuration to an already healthy daemon
review-040.detail: Service installation depends only on the preflight SHA check. When init fills configuration gaps while the daemon is healthy, it never reloads or restarts that daemon. Factory loads its configuration and provider catalog at startup, so the new providers and merge default remain inactive. Reproduction: `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-probes.ts"` printed `healthy-daemon-new-config: {"added":["claude","codex","local-1234"],"effects":["smoke","mcp"],"service":"already set"}`.
review-040.failure_scenario: A daemon is running at the installed SHA. Init detects a new local provider and writes it to config.toml, returns success, but the running daemon cannot route to that provider.

review-040.title: Run setup smoke checks against the effective provider catalog
review-040.detail: The production smoke adapter invokes scripts/smoke.ts main, which discards the configured catalog and constructs checks from static PROVIDERS and MODELS. Detected local providers are never exercised, overridden endpoints are ignored, and both native CLIs are tested even when preflight permits one to be absent. The isolated probe command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-probes.ts"` enumerated smoke rows with a zero execution budget: config contained local-1234, but the output contained only claude, codex, omlx, twilight, openrouter and typesafe rows.
review-040.failure_scenario: Init detects an OpenAI-compatible server on port 1234 and saves it successfully, but never tests an inference against it. A machine with only Claude installed also passes preflight and then runs Codex smoke checks.

review-040.title: Check repository access for newly selected organizations
review-040.detail: The access probe reads only the first repository in the old config. Repositories supplied through --repo or the interactive prompt receive no access check before being persisted; additional configured organizations are also ignored. The probe command `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-setup-probes.ts"` printed `new-repository-access: {"repo":"private/restricted","ghCommands":["gh auth status"],"exit":0}`. With public/accessible followed by org/sso-blocked, it reported gh as ok and only called `gh api repos/public/accessible -i`.
review-040.failure_scenario: A user has valid GitHub authentication but lacks SSO authorization for the organization passed to init --repo. Setup saves the repository and reports success without providing the required SSO fix.

review-040.title: Collect and persist the requested discreet-mode choice
review-040.detail: Discreet mode is replaced with a hardcoded skipped message. Init never asks about it or saves a default, despite this being an explicit setup requirement. Reproduction: `bun --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-discreet-probe.ts"` printed questions for provider enablement, repositories, merge policy and MCP, followed by `"discreet":"skipped: discreet mode: not available yet (#37)"`; no discreet setting was persisted.
review-040.failure_scenario: An interactive user runs init for a repository that requires discreet operation and cannot select that behavior; --yes likewise records no discreet-mode default.

review-042.title: Detect signals executed inside shell expansions
review-042.detail: Double-quoted arguments are treated as opaque strings, and non-interpreter heredocs are discarded entirely. Both can execute command substitutions, so real kill attempts disappear from warnings, the feed, and reports. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\""), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
review-042.failure_scenario: An agent submits echo "$(kill -TERM 123)" or an unquoted cat heredoc containing $(kill -TERM 123). The shell attempts the signal, but neither harness emits a warning.

review-042.title: Preserve executable JavaScript template interpolations
review-042.detail: jsSignal removes entire template literals, including executable ${...} expressions. A process.kill call inside an interpolation is therefore missed in both shell-invoked JavaScript and JavaScript tools. Targeted command: bun --eval 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("node -e '\''console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'\''"), true);'. Output: AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: false !== true.
review-042.failure_scenario: An agent runs node -e 'console.log(`${process.kill(123)}`)'. JavaScript attempts the signal, but the event log and report contain no signal warning.

review-042.title: Provide writable isolated state for the confined Codex CLI
review-042.detail: The new outer profile denies writes outside cwd and scratch, but the CLI still inherits its normal HOME/CODEX_HOME. Normal invocations remain persistent because --ephemeral is added only for privateSession. Codex therefore cannot create its session rollout and other persistent state under ~/.codex. Unlike the corresponding Claude change, this wrapper does not accommodate the CLI's persistence requirements. The substitute smoke executable never attempts those writes.
review-042.failure_scenario: On a host where confinement preflights succeed, a normal tool-enabled Codex invocation starts with privateSession unset and attempts to create its rollout under ~/.codex; the outer write policy denies it and the invocation fails.

review-042.title: Detect executed substitutions inside double-quoted shell arguments
review-042.detail: Double-quoted tokens are treated as opaque literals, although command substitutions inside them execute. Consequently echo "$(kill -TERM 123)" produces no warning, feed item, or report count. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { signalCommand } from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(kill -TERM 123)\""), true, "executed command substitution must be detected");'. Output: AssertionError: executed command substitution must be detected; false !== true.
review-042.failure_scenario: Either harness emits a shell tool call containing echo "$(kill -TERM 123)". The shell executes kill, but signalCommand returns false and no signal warning is recorded.

review-042.title: Detect executable substitutions inside quoted shell arguments
review-042.detail: Double-quoted arguments are treated as opaque tokens, so executable command substitutions are ignored. Unquoted heredoc bodies are also discarded as literal data despite permitting command substitution. Reproduction: bun -e 'import {signalCommand} from "./src/harness/signals.ts"; import {strict as assert} from "node:assert"; assert.equal(signalCommand("echo \"$(pkill -f marker)\""), true)' fails with `AssertionError: false !== true`. This only analyzes the string; it does not execute pkill. Such tool calls produce no signal warning, event-log warning, or run.warning feed item.
review-042.failure_scenario: An agent submits Bash command `echo "$(pkill -f marker)"` or an unquoted heredoc containing `$(kill 123)`. The shell attempts the signal, but signalCommand returns false and the attempt is absent from warning reporting.

Codex initializes its session rollout under CODEX_HOME/sessions before executing the agent; denying that write prevents normal invocations from starting. The substitute CLI tests never exercise this initialization.

review-042.failure_scenario: On a host where confinement preflights succeed, a normal tool-enabled Codex invocation uses ~/.codex outside its permitted write roots and fails during initialization.

"}}); console.log(JSON.stringify(events)); assert.equal(events.some(e => e.type === "warning"), true, "executed kill in unquoted heredoc m
review-042.failure_scenario: An agent submits a Bash command containing an unquoted heredoc with a kill, pkill, or killall command substitution. The signal attempt is absent from warnings and the report count.

review-042.detail:
Double-quoted shell tokens are treated as opaque, and non-interpreter heredocs are discarded entirely. Both can execute command substitutions. Output: 'original: true', 'edited PCM: false', followed by the assertion error. Changi
