review-061.title: Cwd and birth time incorrectly establish process ownership
review-061.detail: Any hidden-environment orphan born after invocation start with a cwd under the worktree is treated as an invocation member, without evidence of ancestry. This kills unrelated processes sharing that directory. A standalone check launched an independent sibling launcher that orphaned a shell in the invocation cwd. Command `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-unrelated-orphan.ts` returned `{"exitCode":0,"unrelatedOrphanAliveAfterReturn":false}`.
review-061.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another worker or user starts a detached platform process in the same checkout. Invocation shutdown kills that unrelated process.

review-061.title: Gate timeout rerun bypasses cleanup retry and recovery
review-061.detail: The second checkoutCommitted call omits retryClean even when implementerIssue is set. If this clean fails, it throws CommandError rather than WorktreeCleanError, so the new recovery handler rethrows it and fails the run. A standalone probe of this call's default behavior, `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-kCikyJ/claude-501/review-clean-retry.ts`, produced `{"errorType":"CommandError","cleanAttempts":1}` for a clean that would succeed on its second attempt.
review-061.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer leaves partial work, gates time out only on the changed revision, and git clean fails once before the gate rerun. Even if final discard succeeds, the run fails instead of retrying cleanup or advancing rounds.

review-061.title: Birth time and working directory do not prove process ownership
review-061.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden-environment process born during the invocation whose cwd is under a supplied root, even without a matching marker, session, group, or ancestor. stopMarkedProcesses then signals it. Another concurrent command or user process can satisfy these conditions. Exact probe command: bun -e 'import {hiddenDarwinProcessMember as member} from "./src/util/processes-darwin.ts"; console.log({unrelatedOrphanSelected:member(42,new Map([[42,1]]),new Set(),100,[process.cwd()],()=>101,()=>({path:process.cwd()}))});'. Output: { unrelatedOrphanSelected: true }.
review-061.failure_scenario: While a Git command runs, another concurrent command launches a detached macOS platform process in the same checkout and its launcher exits. The Git command's teardown selects and kills that unrelated orphan.

review-061.title: Cwd and birth time do not establish ownership of an orphan
review-061.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden-environment process born after invocation start whose cwd is within a captured directory, without proving ancestry or marker ownership. An unrelated launcher can create exactly that state. The standalone native-inspection assertion printed `unrelatedOrphanSelected: true` and failed with `Expected to not contain: 81592; Received: [81592]`. stopMarkedProcesses will send SIGTERM and potentially SIGKILL to that selected process, allowing one invocation to terminate unrelated work.
review-061.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached macOS platform process in the same checkout or captured scratch directory and exits. Invocation cleanup selects and kills that unrelated orphan.

review-061.title: Do not infer process ownership from birth time and cwd
review-061.detail: An unrelated orphan born during an invocation is classified as its descendant solely because it shares the working directory. Cleanup consequently signals processes belonging to other callers. A standalone reproduction launched an independent, unmarked /bin/sleep through a separate launcher while the invocation waited. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-377.test.ts". Output: '(fail) independent orphan survives invocation cleanup', 'Expected: true', 'Received: false'.
review-061.failure_scenario: Another caller launches a detached platform process in the same directory while runProcess is active; its launcher exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated orphan.

review-061.title: Directory-based orphan detection selects unrelated processes
review-061.detail: Birth time, orphan status, and a shared working directory do not establish invocation ownership. This fallback selects unrelated platform processes launched during the invocation, and stopMarkedProcesses then signals them. A standalone reproduction launched an unmarked orphan shell independently of the invocation and scanned with an unrelated marker. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-mSgofg/claude-501/review-orphan.ts. Output: {"unrelatedOrphanSelectedForTermination":true}.
review-061.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another tool launches an orphan platform process in the same checkout directory. Invocation shutdown selects and kills that unrelated process.

review-061.title: Directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
review-061.detail: A newly orphaned platform process is classified as belonging to the invocation solely because it started later and shares its working directory. Shutdown consequently kills unrelated background jobs. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-process-boundaries.test.ts". Output: "invocation exit 0 unrelated orphan alive false", followed by "Expected: true; Received: false". The corresponding base-commit check passes.
review-061.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached /bin/sleep in the same directory and exits. When the invocation finishes, shutdown kills that unrelated orphan.

review-061.title: Preserve process-group membership when descendants replace their environment
review-061.detail: Session/group membership is accepted only when the environment is hidden. A descendant with a visible explicit environment lacking the invocation markers is excluded, even when it remains in the invocation's process group. runProcess then returns successfully while the writer continues running. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/review-process-boundaries.test.ts" --test-name-pattern 'same-group'. Output: "invocation exit 0 same-group descendant alive true", followed by "Expected: false; Received: true". After allowing 100 ms for signal delivery, the same check passes against the base implementation.
review-061.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a background Bun writer with stdio ignored and env: {EXPLICIT_ENV: 'yes'}, then exits. The writer survives shutdown and keeps modifying files during worktree cleanup. A detached platform shell outside the recorded directory roots also survives while writing through absolute pat

review-061.title: Working-directory heuristic selects unrelated processes for termination
review-061.detail: A hidden orphan is classified as an invocation member solely because it was born after invocation start and has a cwd under an invocation root. Neither condition proves ancestry or ownership by that invocation. stopMarkedProcesses sends termination signals to every returned PID. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-SWqZR5/claude-501/review-unrelated-orphan.ts`. Output: `{"selectedForTermination":true}` followed by `error: ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must not be selected for termination`. The check only inspected selection; it did not let the implementation signal the unrelated process.
review-061.failure_scenario: While an invocation is running, another process launches an orphaned /bin/sleep or shell under the same worktree or scratch root. On macOS, shutdown selects that unrelated process and kills it despite its unrelated session and missing invocation marker.

review-061.title: Directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
review-061.detail: The orphan fallback identifies any hidden-environment process born during the invocation and running under its working directory as a member. Another invocation can create precisely such an orphan while remaining alive. Shutdown then kills that unrelated invocation's shell. Reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" overlap. Output: "AssertionError: another invocation shell must survive this invocation shutdown", "false !== true".
review-061.failure_scenario: Two invocations overlap in the same checkout. The second launches a detached /bin/sh through an intermediate launcher that exits. When the first invocation finishes, its process scan selects and kills the second invocation's shell.

review-062.title: Detached shells outside the captured directories still outlive invocation shutdown
review-062.detail: Discovery happens during shutdown, after detached descendants can lose their parent chain. A macOS shell with a hidden environment and cwd outside the captured roots is then omitted, and shutdown returns success. This leaves the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Exact check: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-6edcWS/claude-501/review-process-membership.ts descendant`. Output: `{"mode":"descendant","exitCode":0,"alive":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached background child outlived invocation`. A separate check reproduced this with the invocation environment inherited.
review-062.failure_scenario: The implementer launches a detached background shell in a temporary directory and exits after it starts. The shell can continue writing to absolute worktree paths after runProcess returns and cleanup begins.

review-062.title: Do not claim unrelated orphan processes based on their cwd
review-062.detail: Birth time, orphan status, and a shared directory do not prove invocation ownership. This heuristic adds unrelated processes to the set that receives SIGTERM/SIGKILL. I reproduced this with an independently launched, unmarked /bin/sleep orphan in the invocation's cwd: completing runProcess returned {"exitCode":0,"unrelatedOrphanAlive":false}. A focused assertion also fails. Command: bun -e 'import {hiddenDarwinProcessMember as member} from "./src/util/processes-darwin.ts"; import {strictEqual} from "node:assert"; strictEqual(member(42,new Map([[42,1]]),new Set(),100,[process.cwd()],()=>101,()=>({path:process.cwd()})),false,"an unrelated orphan must not belong to this invocation");'. Output:
review-062.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, a separate launcher starts a background platform process in the same worktree or scratch directory and exits. On macOS, if its environment is hidden, cleanup classifies this unrelated orphan as invocation-owned and kills it.

review-062.title: Working directory does not prove ownership of an orphan process
review-062.detail: The orphan fallback selects any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd is under a recorded directory, even without an invocation marker, matching session/group, or proven ancestry. stopMarkedProcesses then signals that unrelated process. A standalone probe launched an independent orphan and called discovery with an unrelated marker/group. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-process-probes.ts" orphan. Output: {"unrelatedProcessSelected":true}.
review-062.failure_scenario: Another tool starts a background process in the checkout during an invocation and its launcher exits. On macOS, shutdown can classify that unrelated orphan as an invocation descendant and terminate it.

review-062.title: Detached descendants can still write after shutdown reports success
review-062.detail: Discovery begins during termination, so ancestry is already lost when a detached descendant has replaced its environment and its parent has exited. A cwd outside the recorded roots also bypasses the fallback. A real runProcess probe returned successfully while its descendant continued writing into the worktree by absolute path. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-process-probes.ts" escape. Output: {"exitCode":0,"writerAlive":true,"continuedWriting":true}. This escape predates the change but leaves the requested whole-tree shutdown guarantee unmet.
review-062.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached helper with a clean environment and a temporary cwd, then exits. The helper keeps writing to an absolute worktree path after runProcess resolves, allowing cleanup to race with the surviving writer.

review-062.title: Detached children with replaced environments survive shutdown
review-062.detail:
An unmarked detached orphan with a visible, nonempty replacement environment is excluded from the hidden-process fallback. runProcess therefore reports successful shutdown while its child remains alive. Reproduced with:

bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts";const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e",`const c=require("child_process").spawn(process.execPath,["-e","setTimeout(()=>{},5000)"],{detached:true,stdio:"ignore",env:{FOO:"bar"}});c.unref();console.log(c.pid)`],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env});const pid=Number(r.stdout);try{console.log("background alive after return",process.kill(pid,0))}finally{process.kill(pid,"SIGKILL")}'

Output:
background alive after r
review-062.failure_scenario: An implementer's launcher supplies a clean environment to a detached background writer and exits. Shutdown misses the writer, allowing it to race with worktree cleanup—the original failure remains possible.

review-062.title: Detached descendants with replaced environments survive shutdown
review-062.detail: Discovery starts only during shutdown. A descendant that starts a new session with a custom environment and becomes orphaned before inspection has neither a marker nor a proven ancestor. When its environment remains visible, the hidden-process fallback also excludes it. runProcess then reports successful shutdown while the descendant remains alive. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-p4xl5T/claude-501/review-process-tree.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: detached descendant must be gone before runProcess returns` followed by `true !== false`.
review-062.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a detached background writer with env:{PATH:process.env.PATH,CUSTOM_ENV:'yes'}, then exits. The writer is orphaned before shutdown inspection and continues modifying files during cleanup.

review-062.title: Working directory does not prove an orphan belongs to the invocation
review-062.detail: The new orphan fallback claims unrelated processes based solely on birth time and cwd, then signals them. A control process launched independently of the invocation was killed; it survives against the base. Exact command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-BlBx7g/claude-501/review377-zhdzifu0/unrelated.ts`. Output: `{"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedOrphanSurvived":false}` followed by `error: ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup` (exit 1).
review-062.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts a detached native process in the same directory and exits. The unrelated process becomes an orphan, satisfies this heuristic, and is terminated during invocation shutdown.

review-062.title: Detached native descendants can still write after confirmed shutdown
review-062.detail: The fallback misses reparented native descendants whose cwd is outside the recorded roots. With an inherited environment, a detached /bin/sh running from / wrote into the worktree after runProcess returned success. Exact command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-BlBx7g/claude-501/review377-zhdzifu0/escaped.ts`. Output: `{"invocationExit":0,"descendantWroteAfterReturn":true}` followed by `error: ASSERTION FAILED: descendant wrote into worktree after invocation returned` (exit 1). The base also fails this check, so this is an existing escape left unresolved by the requested whole-process-tree fix.
review-062.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached shell from another directory, with inherited environment and redirected stdio, then exits. The shell is reparented before shutdown inspection and later writes to an absolute worktree path while cleanup or the next round proceeds.

review-062.title: Directory overlap does not prove process ownership
review-062.detail: A hidden orphan is classified as belonging to an invocation solely because it was born after invocation start and shares its directory. This kills unrelated processes without marker or ancestry evidence. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-process-probe.ts"`. Output: `{"result":0,"orphanPid":6791,"unrelatedOrphanAlive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup`.
review-062.failure_scenario: While runProcess is active, an independent launcher starts a detached /bin/sleep with an empty environment in the same directory and exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated orphan.

review-062.title: Detached descendants outside the captured directories still survive
review-062.detail: The requested whole-process-tree guarantee remains unmet. A detached descendant with no visible marker, reparented before inspection and running outside the captured directories, is omitted; runProcess returns success while it remains alive. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-escaped-probe.ts"`. Output: `{"result":0,"descendantPid":9666,"descendantAlive":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached descendant must be gone before runProcess returns`. The same probe against the base confirmed this is a pre-existing failure that the requested fix leaves unresolved.
review-062.failure_scenario: An invocation spawns a detached process with an empty environment and cwd outside the worktree, then exits. That descendant can continue writing into the worktree through absolute paths while cleanup proceeds.

review-062.title: Working-directory matching kills unrelated orphan processes
review-062.detail: A hidden orphan born during an invocation is treated as its descendant solely because its cwd is inside the invocation directory. This does not establish ancestry. I launched an independent process from the reviewer, orphaned it while an invocation was running, and observed shutdown kill it. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" unrelated`. Output: `{"mode":"unrelated","exitCode":0,"alive":false}` followed by `error: unrelated orphan was killed`.
review-062.failure_scenario: An unrelated launcher starts a detached, environment-hidden process in the same checkout during an invocation and exits. Invocation shutdown classifies that orphan as owned and kills it.

review-062.title: Detached descendants can still survive confirmed shutdown
review-062.detail: Discovery starts at termination, so a detached descendant whose parent has exited, whose environment lacks the marker, and whose cwd is outside the recorded roots is missed. runProcess returns successfully while it remains alive, leaving the requested whole-tree guarantee unmet. Command: `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" leak`. Output: `{"mode":"leak","exitCode":0,"alive":true}` followed by `error: descendant survived confirmed shutdown`. The fixture spawned detached `/bin/sleep` with `env:{}` and cwd TMPDIR.
review-062.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a detached writer with a replacement environment and temporary cwd, then exits. The writer uses absolute paths into the checkout and continues writing while cleanup runs.

review-063.title: Working directory and birth time do not establish process ownership
review-063.detail: The orphan fallback selects unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. Reproduced with an independently launched, detached, empty-environment sleep process. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-SaMTh6/claude-501/review-377.ULtj4q/process-ownership.ts`. Output: `unrelatedProcessSurvived: false (expected true)`. Finishing an ordinary command killed the unrelated process.
review-063.failure_scenario: Another run or user launches an orphan with an empty or hidden environment in the same directory while a factory command is running. The factory kills it when its own command finishes.

review-063.title: Shutdown is confirmed while detached descendants remain alive
review-063.detail: Discovery misses a detached descendant that clears its environment and changes cwd outside the recorded roots before its parent exits. The new shutdown loop then reports success. Command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-SaMTh6/claude-501/review-377.ULtj4q/process-ownership.ts`. Output: `descendantSurvived: true (expected false)`. The fixture launches the descendant from inside runProcess with env={}, cwd='/', detached=true and stdio='ignore'.
review-063.failure_scenario: An implementer backgrounds a detached tool with a sanitized environment and a different cwd. That tool continues writing to absolute worktree paths after runProcess returns, racing cleanup.

review-063.title: The gate timeout rerun bypasses cleanup recovery
review-063.detail: Only the initial checkoutCommitted call receives retryClean. If gates time out, the second call at line 1109 uses the default false. Its clean failure remains a CommandError, so the catch at line 1164 rejects it instead of treating it as a failed implement round. A transient cleanup failure can therefore still fail the whole run after a stuck implementer.
review-063.failure_scenario: A stuck implement round reaches gates; the first cleanup succeeds; gates time out; the clean before the gate rerun fails once; final discard succeeds. The run fails without retrying that clean or advancing to another implement round.

review-063.title: Do not infer process ownership from working directory and birth time
review-063.detail: The orphan fallback claims unrelated processes merely because they started during the invocation and share its working directory. Cleanup then signals those processes. A direct reproduction launched an independent orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess was active. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts". Output: {"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedPid":34184,"unrelatedAlive":false}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup'.
review-063.failure_scenario: Another task or user starts a detached process in the same checkout while an invocation runs; its launcher exits. Invocation cleanup kills that unrelated process.

review-063.title: Detached descendants can still outlive invocation cleanup
review-063.detail: Discovery loses descendants that detach, replace their environment, and change directory outside the invocation roots before their parent exits. runProcess then reports successful termination while the child continues writing into the worktree by absolute path. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-escape.ts". Output: {"invocationExit":0,"descendantPid":39246,"descendantAlive":true}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: invocation descendant must be stopped before runProcess returns'. This leaves the original cleanup race possible and violates the whole-process-tree requirement.
review-063.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached background shell with a clean environment and an external working directory. The shell writes to an absolute worktree path, and the implementer exits. Cleanup proceeds while the writer remains alive.

review-063.title: Working directory does not prove ownership of an orphan
review-063.detail: The orphan fallback claims any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd matches an invocation directory, even without ancestry or an invocation marker. This kills unrelated processes. A temporary fixture launched an unrelated orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess was active. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" unrelated. Output: {"case":"unrelated","alive":false,"bytesWrittenAfterReturn":0}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: unrelated orphan must survive invocation cleanup' (exit 1).
review-063.failure_scenario: Another invocation or user launches a detached, environment-cleared process in the same worktree after this invocation starts. Its parent exits. Finishing this invocation kills that unrelated orphan.

review-063.title: Detached descendants can survive confirmed shutdown
review-063.detail: Discovery misses descendants that clear their environment, create a separate session, and leave the invocation directories before their parent exits. runProcess then returns successfully while they continue writing into the worktree through absolute paths. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts" descendant. Output: {"case":"descendant","alive":true,"bytesWrittenAfterReturn":2}, followed by 'ASSERTION FAILED: invocation descendant must stop before runProcess returns' (exit 1). This preserves the cleanup race the request requires fixing.
review-063.failure_scenario: An implementer starts a detached background writer with env {}, cwd /private/tmp, and an absolute output path inside the worktree, then exits. Cleanup starts while the writer remains alive.

review-063.title: Do not infer process ownership from an orphan's working directory
review-063.detail:
An unrelated orphan born during an invocation is classified as its descendant when it shares the working directory. Shutdown consequently signals processes belonging to other invocations or the user. Reproduced with this exact command:
bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; import {spawnSync} from "node:child_process"; let sibling; try { const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","console.log(\"ready\"); setTimeout(()=>{},300)"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env,onStdoutLine:()=>{const s=spawnSync(process.execPath,["-e","const c=require(\"node:child_process\").spawn(\"/bin/sleep\",[\"30\"],{env:{},detached:true,stdio:\"ignore\"}); console.log(c.pid); c.unref()"],{en
review-063.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, an independent launcher starts a detached process with an empty environment in the same checkout and exits. Finishing the invocation kills that unrelated process.

review-063.title: Actual descendants can still outlive successful invocation shutdown
review-063.detail:
The acknowledged fallback limitation leaves the requested whole-tree shutdown incomplete: a detached descendant with a replaced environment and a different cwd survives, while runProcess returns success and permits cleanup. Reproduced with this exact command:
bun -e 'import {runProcess} from "./src/util/proc.ts"; let pid; try {const r=await runProcess({cmd:[process.execPath,"-e","const c=require(\"node:child_process\").spawn(\"/bin/sleep\",[\"30\"],{cwd:\"/\",env:{},detached:true,stdio:\"ignore\"}); console.log(c.pid); c.unref()"],cwd:process.cwd(),env:process.env}); pid=Number(r.stdout.trim()); let alive=true; try{process.kill(pid,0)}catch{alive=false} console.log("invocation exit:",r.exitC
review-063.failure_scenario: An implementer launches a detached writer with env:{} and cwd outside the checkout, writing into the checkout through an absolute path. The implementer exits; shutdown reports success while the writer continues racing cleanup.

review-063.title: Working directory and birth time do not prove process ownership
review-063.detail: The orphan fallback selects unrelated processes solely because they were born during the invocation and share its working directory. Shutdown then signals them. A separate, unmarked launcher reproduced this with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-orphan.ts"`: output was `{"invocationExit":0,"unrelatedControlPid":33510,"unrelatedControlAlive":false}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: an invocation killed an orphan started by a separate launcher without invocation markers`.
review-063.failure_scenario: While an invocation runs, another launcher starts an unmarked background shell in the same checkout and exits. Invocation shutdown kills that unrelated shell.

review-063.title: Children that replace their environment can escape shutdown
review-063.detail: Linux discovery requires inherited environment markers and removes the previous process-group kill, so even ordinary same-group children with a replaced environment can survive. Darwin also misses detached descendants with a nonempty replacement environment once their parent exits. `bun "$TMPDIR/review-scrubbed.ts"` reproduced the Darwin case: `{"invocationExit":0,"writerPid":37518,"writerAliveAfterReturn":true}`, followed by `ASSERTION FAILED: detached descendant with a replaced environment outlived invocation`. Shutdown reports success while the writer remains active.
review-063.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a background writer with `env: { PATH: process.env.PATH }` and redirected stdio, then exits. The writer loses the markers, survives shutdown, and continues modifying files during cleanup.

review-063.title: Shutdown can succeed while a background descendant remains alive
review-063.detail: Discovery misses a detached descendant that clears its environment and changes cwd outside the invocation roots. After its parent exits, two empty scans confirm shutdown and permit cleanup despite the surviving process. A temporary fixture spawning such a shell reproduced this with `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377.ts"`: output was `{"exitCode":0,"descendantAlive":true}`.
review-063.failure_scenario: An implementer spawns a detached writer with env: {}, changes its cwd to another directory, and exits or is stopped. The writer continues modifying worktree files by absolute path after runProcess resolves.

review-063.title: Directory overlap incorrectly establishes ownership of unrelated processes
review-063.detail: A hidden orphan is selected solely because it was born during the invocation and has a cwd under an invocation root. Neither condition proves ancestry. An independent launcher created an unmarked orphan while runProcess was active in the same directory; finishing that invocation killed the independent process. `bun "$TMPDIR/review-377-isolation.ts"` printed `invocation exit: 0` and `independent control alive: false`.
review-063.failure_scenario: Two concurrent commands use the same checkout. One creates an environment-cleared detached child. When the other command finishes, its cleanup claims and kills that child, interrupting work owned by another invocation.

review-063.title: Require ownership evidence before killing an orphan
review-063.detail: An empty-environment orphan is classified as belonging to this invocation solely because it was born after invocation start and its cwd is inside an invocation directory. An independent process can satisfy both conditions. I reproduced this with a sibling launcher creating an unrelated shell orphan in the same cwd: finishing runProcess killed that orphan. Command: TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501 bun test /private/tmp/lr-sjhTlZ/claude-501/review-boundary.test.ts. Output included '(fail) independent hidden orphan in same cwd must survive' and 'SystemError: kill() failed: ESRCH: No such process'.
review-063.failure_scenario: While invocation A is running, an independent launcher starts an empty-environment detached process in A's cwd and exits. A's shutdown discovers the orphan and kills it despite having no ownership relationship.

review-063.title: Stop detached descendants with reduced environments
review-063.detail: Detached descendants that replace their environment with a nonempty reduced environment lose the markers and session/group membership. After reparenting, they also miss the orphan fallback because hidden only includes processes with no visible environment. Shutdown then reports success while the writer remains alive. The same boundary-test command reported 'invocation exitCode: 0 writer alive: true', followed by '(fail) scrubbed detached orphan must stop before invocation returns' and 'Received function did not throw'. This leaves cleanup exposed to the original background-writer race.
review-063.failure_scenario: An invocation spawns a detached background writer with env: { PATH: process.env.PATH } and stdio: 'ignore', waits until it writes, then exits. runProcess resolves successfully while the writer continues modifying the worktree.

review-063.title: Working-directory overlap does not establish process ownership
review-063.detail: The orphan fallback claims any hidden process born during the invocation whose cwd lies under its working directory. An unrelated invocation or user process can meet all these conditions and receive SIGTERM/SIGKILL. A standalone probe starts an independent orphan from the reviewer process while runProcess is active, using the same cwd and an empty environment. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-377.ts" ownership. Output includes `ownership: alive=false` and `AssertionError: unrelated orphan must survive` (`false !== true`).
review-063.failure_scenario: Two concurrent operations share a checkout. One creates an orphan with an empty or hidden environment after the other starts. Finishing the other operation kills that unrelated orphan.

review-063.title: Detached descendants with replacement environments survive shutdown
review-063.detail: Discovery starts only during shutdown. A detached writer whose intermediate parent has exited has no observable ancestry or original session membership. If its replacement environment contains PATH but no invocation marker, it also bypasses the hidden-process fallback. runProcess then reports success while the writer remains alive. Command: bun "$TMPDIR/limitless-review-377.ts" descendant. Output includes `descendant: alive=true` and `AssertionError: invocation descendant must be stopped` (`true !== false`). The same probe fails against the base implementation, so this is an existing limitation left unresolved by the explicit whole-tree shutdown requirement.
review-063.failure_scenario: The implementer launches an intermediary that starts a detached background writer with env={PATH: ...} and exits. The implementer subsequently ends. Shutdown returns successfully and cleanup begins while the writer continues modifying the checkout.

review-064.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
review-064.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second connection idle timeout. This endpoint uses JSON responses and awaits the entire subprocess result before returning any bytes, so verification commands exceeding that interval lose their MCP connection even when the subprocess produces output. The request signal is included in the subprocess cancellation signal, so disconnecting can also terminate the test. Increasing the CLI tool timeout does not change this server timeout.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite taking 20 seconds with timeoutMs set to 180000. The HTTP connection times out around 10 seconds before the command result is returned, causing a tool transport failure instead of successful verification.

review-064.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running commands
review-064.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This bridge buffers command output and sends its JSON response only after executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands taking longer than that can lose their HTTP connection despite the much larger configured command and MCP timeouts. The request signal also participates in command cancellation, so the disconnect can terminate verification.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier calls the command tool with `sleep 15; echo passed` and timeoutMs/idleTimeoutMs of 180000. The HTTP connection times out before the successful command result can return.

review-064.title: Preserve installed Rust toolchain discovery when replacing HOME
review-064.detail: Reader commands replace HOME with empty scratch without preserving RUSTUP_HOME. Standard rustup installations consequently lose their default compiler, although gates explicitly preserve RUSTUP_HOME in runConfined. Reproduced with `env HOME="$TMPDIR" rustup show active-toolchain`, which outputs `error: no active toolchain`. Adding `RUSTUP_HOME="$HOME/.rustup"` returns `stable-aarch64-apple-darwin (default)`.
review-064.failure_scenario: A Rust repository uses a standard rustup installation with no explicit RUSTUP_HOME environment variable. Its cargo tests pass gates, but the verifier's reader command cannot discover the installed compiler after HOME changes to scratch, blocking verification.

review-064.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for verification commands
review-064.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint buffers its JSON response until executeReaderCommand finishes, so commands lasting longer than 10 seconds lose their HTTP connection regardless of the configured subprocess and MCP tool timeouts. The request abort signal also feeds into subprocess cancellation. Ordinary verification suites can therefore still fail as environment-blocked.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier calls the reader command tool with a test suite that takes 20 seconds. No HTTP response data is sent during execution, so Bun closes the connection after approximately 10 seconds and the verifier receives a transport failure instead of the test result.

review-064.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long verification commands
review-064.detail: Bun.serve retains its default 10-second idle timeout. The MCP transport uses enableJsonResponse, so no response bytes are sent while executeReaderCommand runs. Commands lasting beyond that timeout can lose their HTTP connection, which also aborts the subprocess through req.signal. Increasing MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT or tool_timeout_sec does not change this server timeout.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite taking 15 seconds with timeoutMs set to 180000. The MCP connection times out before the test completes, causing a tool failure or cancellation instead of returning the test result.

review-064.title: Disable the MCP server's default HTTP idle timeout
review-064.detail: Bun.serve retains its default 10-second idle timeout. The JSON MCP transport sends no response until executeReaderCommand completes, so commands lasting longer than that can lose their connection despite the much larger configured command timeout. Subprocess stdout does not keep this HTTP connection active. The disconnect also aborts req.signal, which is passed to the command, potentially terminating otherwise successful verification.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a test suite that takes 20 seconds. The MCP connection remains idle while the subprocess runs and closes around 10 seconds, causing a tool transport error or command cancellation instead of returning the test result.

review-064.title: Restrict loopback binding to ephemeral ports
review-064.detail: The wildcard network-bind rule permits binding any loopback TCP port. Restrictions on network-inbound prevent listening on service ports, but binding alone reserves a port and can prevent other local processes from using it. This violates the requested ephemeral-only restriction. The new test combines bind and listen, so a denial at listen hides the successful prohibited bind.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier command binds an available 127.0.0.1:12345 socket and keeps it open without calling listen. Another local process attempting to start a service on that address receives EADDRINUSE despite the port being outside the permitted ephemeral range.

review-064.title: Disable the HTTP idle timeout for long-running reader commands
review-064.detail: Bun.serve defaults to a 10-second idle timeout. This endpoint uses enableJsonResponse and awaits the entire command before sending its response, so even commands producing subprocess output send no HTTP traffic while running. Commands exceeding the HTTP idle window lose their connection; req.signal also participates in command cancellation. The configured command and MCP timeouts therefore cannot protect ordinary longer test runs.
review-064.failure_scenario: A verifier invokes a local-server test suite taking 30 seconds with timeoutMs and idleTimeoutMs both set to 180000. The MCP connection times out before the command returns, preventing the verifier from receiving the test result.

review-065.title: Require positive test execution evidence for targeted commands
review-065.detail: The exact-file branch accepts a successful process whenever its output lacks failure or skip markers, even with no passing tests. Confirmed that Bun exits 0 and emits only its version and file header when a test module calls process.exit(0). Those actual output bytes are accepted as coverage. Targeted command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-AAmrsP/claude-501/review-gate-evidence.ts zero`. Output: `expected blocked; actual met`, followed by `error: Unverified criterion was marked met`.
review-065.failure_scenario: A targeted loopback test exits successfully during initialization before registering or executing tests. Its gate passes with empty passedFiles, and a blocked verifier criterion is nevertheless converted to met.

review-065.title: Check tested working-tree bytes before recording commit provenance
review-065.detail: Evidence eligibility checks only HEAD, after discardChanges has erased gate modifications. Setup commands and earlier checks can modify tracked source or tests without changing HEAD. Subsequent tests then pass against those modified bytes, but the new evidence attributes that pass to the original commit and can override a blocked independent verification.
review-065.failure_scenario: A configured setup or fixing check rewrites a tracked source file so the loopback test passes. Gates succeed, discardChanges restores the broken committed file, and HEAD remains unchanged. When the reader cannot run the test, its blocked result becomes met using evidence from the repaired working tr

review-065.title: Require positive coverage for every explicitly requested file
review-065.detail: The exact-command shortcut accepts matching file arguments without checking that each file ran. Bun treats these arguments as filters and exits successfully when one matches and another is missing. Command: bun test "$TMPDIR/limitless-383-review.test.ts". The missing-file regression printed `gate exit: 0 ran: Ran 1 test across 1 file.` and failed with `Expected: "blocked", Received: "met"`.
review-065.failure_scenario: Both the gate and criterion request `bun test ./present.test.ts ./missing.test.ts`. Only present.test.ts exists and passes. The verifier reports blocked, but the factory certifies both requested files.

review-065.title: Partial command parsing can approve tests that never ran
review-065.detail: The regex extracts only a command prefix and silently discards unsupported syntax or remaining instructions. For `bun test "test/loopback.test.ts"`, it extracts bare `bun test`, allowing any passing file to satisfy the criterion. It also ignores additional verification steps after a newline. Targeted command: `bun test "$TMPDIR/verifier-evidence-review.test.ts"`. Both cases failed with `Expected: "blocked"; Received: "met"` (0 pass, 2 fail).
review-065.failure_scenario: The criterion requests `bun test "test/loopback.test.ts"`, the verifier reports a sandbox block, and gate output contains only `test/unrelated.test.ts:\n(pass) unrelated`. The factory marks the criterion met despite never running the requested file.

review-065.title: Interrupted gate completion permanently disables evidence on resume
review-065.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks and gateEvidence before marking the gate stage succeeded. A crash between those writes leaves cached successful checks referencing a running stage, which scheduler recovery marks cancelled. On resume, the gates cache bypasses execution, but this new status check rejects its evidence. Neither verification attempt repairs or reruns the gates, so an otherwise passing run ends as environment-blocked.
review-065.failure_scenario: The daemon stops after the gates checkpoint saves but before finishStage records success. It restarts on the same SHA, reuses cached gates, and both reader verification attempts encounter the loopback restriction. Successful gate evidence is rejected and the run becomes needs_human.

review-065.title: The targeted-command shortcut ignores evidence that the requested file never passed
review-065.detail:
When selected and requested arguments match, the shortcut returns true without checking passedFiles—even when retained coverage explicitly contains only another file. Bun treats an argument without ./ as a substring filter. In a temporary fixture containing an empty test/loopback.test.ts and a passing nested/test/loopback.test.ts, the exact command `bun test test/loopback.test.ts` exited 0 with output: `test/loopback.test.ts:

nested/test/loopback.test.ts:
(pass) unrelated [0.03ms]

 1 pass
 0 fail
 1 expect() calls
Ran 1 test across 2 files.` Applying that result produced `SUBSTITUTED STATUS: met` and failed the assertion `ASSERTION FAILED: required file ran zero tests; only nested/
review-065.failure_scenario: The requested test file registers no tests, while a different file matching the same Bun substring filter passes. The verifier cannot execute the requested test, but the factory marks its criterion met using the unrelated passing file.

review-065.title: Partial test coverage incorrectly satisfies an entire blocked criterion
review-065.detail: The matcher extracts a Bun command from verification instructions and ignores additional checks. applyGateEvidence then marks the entire criterion met without checking whether the blocked operation was covered. Reproduction command: `TMPDIR=/private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501 TMP=/private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501 TEMP=/private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501 bun /private/tmp/lr-EZtPeE/claude-501/review-gate-coverage.ts`. Output: `AssertionError: Expected values to be strictly equal: 'met' !== 'blocked'`.
review-065.failure_scenario: A criterion says: 'Run `bun test test/loopback.test.ts`. Then run a separate outbound-denial probe.' Gates pass the loopback file, while the verifier reports the separate probe blocked by EPERM. The factory marks the criterion met despite having no evidence for outbound denial, potentially allowing

review-066.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the loopback workaround
review-066.detail:
passed() rejects any check containing a skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to satisfy passed(). Consequently, a successfully executed loopback test cannot supply evidence when an unrelated platform test is skipped. This repository deliberately skips tests when LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, which runConfined sets, so its normal gates cannot supply the intended evidence. Reproduction: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod-preload.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-boundaries.test.ts". The assertion 'an unrelated platform skip must not invalidate a passing loopback file' failed with:
Expected: "met"
Received: "blocked"
review-066.failure_scenario: The confined bun test gate exits zero and records test/loopback.test.ts in passedFiles, while a separate nested-Seatbelt test is skipped. The verifier cannot bind loopback, reports blocked, and the engine still ends verification as needs_human despite passing coverage of the requested test.

review-066.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable the loopback fallback
review-066.detail: The clean-result predicate rejects any skipped file, and applyGateEvidence requires every gate to satisfy it. Limitless deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests inside confined gates, so its successful suite cannot attest to a fully passing loopback test in another file. The reported verification block therefore remains for this repository. Reproduction command: bun test --preload "$TMPDIR/review-zod.ts" "$TMPDIR/review-gate-repro.test.ts". Output: '(fail) unrelated skipped file', 'Expected: "met"', 'Received: "blocked"'. The temporary preload selects the installed Zod v4.
review-066.failure_scenario: Confined bun test passes test/loopback.test.ts but skips a nested Seatbelt test in test/sandbox.test.ts. The reader cannot bind loopback, and the engine rejects the otherwise valid gate evidence, leaving verification blocked.

review-066.title: Unrelated skipped tests disable all gate evidence
review-066.detail: passed() rejects any check containing skipped files, and applyGateEvidence requires every check to pass this predicate. Consequently, a passing loopback test cannot supply evidence when an unrelated test is skipped. This repository deliberately skips real Seatbelt tests under LIMITLESS_CONFINED=1, which runConfined always sets, so ordinary confined suite results retain the original verification blockage. review-083.title: Preserve reftable storage when constructing the isolated repository
review-083.detail: The isolated repository copies only objects, refs and packed-refs, then declares repository format 0. It omits reftable storage and `extensions.refStorage`, so source references cannot resolve in a reftable repository. In a fixture created with `git init --ref-format=reftable`, `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push --no-follow-tags "$url" HEAD:refs/heads/using-head` returned 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`; the same Git push without the wrapper succeeded. Normal delivery still calls pushBranch with `HEAD` in src/pipeline/engine.ts.
review-083.failure_scenario: A factory repository uses reftable storage, for example through trusted global init.defaultRefFormat configuration. Normal delivery pushes HEAD through the wrapper and fails despite a valid commit and reachable local remote.

review-083.title: The SSH default overrides trusted GIT_SSH
review-083.detail: When core.sshCommand is unset, injecting core.sshCommand=ssh overrides Git's existing GIT_SSH environment setting. A network-free probe used GIT_SSH to run a local receive-pack: `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/before"` succeeded, while `bash scripts/push-git.sh git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null push "$destination" "$sha:refs/heads/after"` exited 128 with `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` The invocation markers were `trusted` followed by `fallback`, proving the wrapper bypassed GIT_SSH.
review-083.failure_scenario: An installation supplies its SSH identity or authentication wrapper through GIT_SSH and has no global core.sshCommand. Factory pushes now invoke plain ssh and fail authentication.

review-083.title: Preserve the repository's reference storage format
review-083.detail: The isolated directory preserves objects and file-based refs but omits reftable storage and extensions.refStorage. Reproduced in a repository initialized with `git init --ref-format=reftable`: a normal file-URL push of `HEAD:refs/heads/default-baseline` succeeded, while the equivalent push through this helper exited 1 with `error: src refspec HEAD does not match any`. pushBranch accepts HEAD by default, and the pipeline also explicitly passes HEAD on a delivery path.
review-083.failure_scenario: Delivery pushes HEAD from a reftable repository. The helper makes Git interpret its administration as file-based refs, so HEAD cannot resolve and delivery fails despite a valid source commit.

review-083.title: Reconstructed administration loses reftable references
review-083.detail: The temporary common directory preserves only files-based refs and object-format metadata. It omits extensions.refStorage and reftable storage. Production delivery still passes HEAD in several paths.

review-083.title: Retain reftable storage when constructing the isolated repository
review-083.detail: The isolated directory exposes only objects, refs and packed-refs, and its config omits extensions.refStorage. Reftable repositories consequently lose their readable refs. review-084.detail: Neither pushBranch nor pushExistingBranch receives the requested protection. Both still consume repository-scoped command settings through worktreeGit. review-090.title: Missing results no longer count while the invocation runs
review-090.detail: Calls awaiting results are excluded from counting, and an unresolved call also blocks later completions of its key. Reproduction command: bun -e 'import { strict as assert } from "node:assert"; import { LoopDetector } from "./src/harness/types.ts"; const d = new LoopDetector(100); let reason = null; for (let i=0; i<6; i++) reason=d.observe("shell", {command:"poll"}, String(i)); for (let i=0; i<12; i++) d.observe("Read", {path:i}, `read-${i}`); assert.equal(d.finish(), "repeated the same shell call 6 times");' Output: AssertionError, actual n

review-090.failure_scenario: An agent issues six identical shell calls with distinct IDs and no results. It continues running instead of stopping; twelve subsequent unrelated calls evict those entries, and finish() returns null.

review-091.title: Out-of-order results can stop progressing parallel calls

review-080.detail: `textAt` sets `binary: bytes.includes(0) || bytes.includes(Buffer.from("%PDF-"))`. This matches the five bytes anywhere in the blob, not only at the start of a PDF. That explains the factory audit flags on this review. The issue predates this diff and the request did not ask for it, but
review-080.failure_scenario: Run `diffSince(repo, c033a437…)` on this change. It returns `binaryPaths: ["src/git/repos.ts","test/git-integrity.test.ts"]` even though both are 100644 text files with no NUL or control bytes, so `auditDiff` blocks them as `[binary-content]` unless the request includes `Allow: binary`.

review-080.title: Text files that contain the literal "%PDF-" are classified as binary and reported as having NUL bytes
review-080.detail: textAt sets `binary: bytes.includes(0) || bytes.includes(Buffer.from("%PDF-"))` for every blob, and binary paths are dropped from `raw`. So any edited text source that mentions "%PDF-" anywhere ends up in binaryPaths through the `!afterText.raw.has(path) && !inert.has(path)` branch. The audit then tells the author the file has "binary bytes, such as a NUL". This is why the automated audit flagged both files in this very change: both contain "%PDF-" and neither contains a NUL. It is the same wild-goose chase the request describes, from a different trigger. This predates the diff and is outside the request's scope.
review-080.failure_scenario: Probe test: commit code.ts as `const a = 1;\n`, then edit it to add `const m = "%PDF-";`. diffSince reports binaryPaths ["code.ts"] on both base and HEAD. The same happens to src/git/repos.ts and test/git-integrity.test.ts in this change.

review-080.title: Replacing a regular file with a same-blob symlink is no longer flagged
review-080.detail: modeRequiresAllowance is also true when the mode changes but the blob ID stays the same. That includes 100644 -> 120000, a regular file replaced by a symlink with identical content. On base this was flagged, misleadingly, as binary content. With the new INERT_MEDIA_PATH guard it passes silently unless the name looks like media. New symlinks and symlinks with a changed target were never flagged on base either, so this is not a new hole. It is only an incidental check that went away without anyone deciding to remove it.
review-080.failure_scenario: Commit link.sh as a regular file containing "target.sh", then replace it with a symlink to target.sh. Base: binaryPaths ["link.sh"]. HEAD: [].

review-119.title: Raw diagnostics become agent-readable after rollback
review-119.detail: Raw text persists in the shared SQLite database, but its read protection exists only in the new harness code. After rollback, the base release's editor profiles permit database reads: its Seatbelt profile has `(allow default)` and no read denial. The additive migration deliberately preserves these rows. Running `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` produced `{"probe":"rollback database boundary","raw":{"text":"RAW_OWNER_HOLDOUT_MARKER"},"allowsDefault":true,"hasReadDenial":false}`. Real Seatbelt execution was unavailable inside this sandbox; the persisted row and base profile were checked directly.
review-119.failure_scenario: The new release records verifier diagnostics, deployment rolls back to the base release, and an implementing agent reads owner_diagnostics directly from the database using its permitted filesystem access.

review-119.title: Capture original thinking events before clipping
review-119.detail: The owner copy is assembled from the normalized `message`. For thinking events, that message has already been clipped to 2,000 characters, so the new owner record cannot recover the full original diagnostic. A focused probe executed the actual onAgentEvent method with private text near the beginning and a diagnostic tail beyond the limit. `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` produced `{"probe":"raw thinking event","inputLength":2136,"storedLength":2000,"tailPreserved":false}`.
review-119.failure_scenario: A verifier emits a thinking event longer than 2,000 characters containing holdout text and useful diagnostic information near its end. show/logs display only the clipped owner copy.

review-119.title: Prevent diagnostic ID reuse behind follow cursors
review-119.detail: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY permits SQLite to reuse deleted maximum IDs. Debug-event cleanup cascades into this table, while logs -f advances using `id > diagnosticsAfter`. A new diagnostic can therefore receive an already-consumed ID and never print. `bun "$TMPDIR/owner-review-probes.ts"` reproduced cursor 1, deletion through deleteOldDebugEvents, a new run-error row with id 1, and `followRows:[]`.
review-119.failure_scenario: logs -f consumes the latest diagnostic, associated with a debug event. GC removes that event and diagnostic (readily reproducible with debug_event_days = 0), then a new error diagnostic reuses its ID and is skipped by subsequent polling.

review-119.title: Preview code can read and publish the new owner-only table
review-119.detail: The database read denials cover harnesses and confined gates, but preview builds, seeds and servers execute checkout code through unconfined runProcess/spawn in src/pipeline/preview.ts. An implementer can therefore change an existing preview build script to query owner_diagnostics, print its contents to stderr and exit unsuccessfully. startPreview includes that stderr in its exception; the engine then publishes it through ordinary run errors and events. Targeted reproduction command: bun "$TMPDIR/owner-preview-review.ts". With only socket allocation substituted because this sandbox cannot bind ports, it printed "Error: Preview build failed: PRIVATE_OWNER_PREVIEW_423" and failed with "Asserti
review-119.failure_scenario: A repository already has preview configuration. After any invocation stores owner diagnostics, an implementer edits the script invoked by preview.build to read the factory database and emit owner_diagnostics.text before exiting 1. The raw text becomes an ordinary preview failure visible through REST

review-119.title: Preserve full event text before clipping the public message
review-119.detail: The new owner copy uses the message passed to add(), but thinking events already slice ev.text to 2,000 characters. Consequently, the supposedly raw diagnostic permanently loses its suffix. Targeted command: bun -e 'import { mock } from "bun:test"; mock.module(`${process.cwd()}/src/pipeline/schemas.ts`, () => ({renderSpec:()=>"", citationInSource:()=>false, citedRequirement:()=>null, requirementEntries:()=>[], requirementSource:()=>"", rowKind:()=>"unknown"})); const {RunContext}=await import("./src/pipeline/context.ts"); const copies=[]; const ctx=Object.create(RunContext.prototype); ctx.run={id:"test-run"}; ctx.deps={store:{addEvent:(e)=>({...e,id:1}),recordOwnerDiagnostic:(d,p)=>{if(d.tex
review-119.failure_scenario: A verifier emits a thinking event exceeding 2,000 characters that contains holdout text. Its owner diagnostic contains only the first 2,000 characters, so show/logs cannot display the full original event.

review-127.title: Handle interrupted gate completion before rejecting cached evidence
review-127.detail: RunContext.stage persists completedChecks.values.gates before calling finishStage(..., "succeeded"). If the daemon stops between those writes, restart reuses the cached gate result without executing or completing that stage. Its recorded status remains non-succeeded, so this new guard refuses delivery even though HEAD is unchanged and subsequent audit, review and verification pass. This introduces a needs_human outcome for an ordinary resumable run.
review-127.failure_scenario: Stop the daemon after context.ts persists completedChecks.values.gates but before finishStage marks that gate stage succeeded. Restart without changing HEAD. The cached gate result is reused, but delivery throws DeliveryHeadError because stage.status is not succeeded.

review-127.title: Errors before the guard can still push through draft fallback
review-127.detail: The first guard runs after the resumed-delivery GitHub lookup. If that lookup throws, executeScopedRun enters deliverVerifiedDraft because the error is not DeliveryHeadError. That function pushes lastVerifiedSha without calling the shared guard. Thus an amended HEAD can still cause a push and draft creation rather than the required refusal naming both SHAs. The fallback suppression only covers mismatches that execution actually reaches.
review-127.failure_scenario: A new-PR run stops at stage:deliver:before and its HEAD is amended. On resume, the initial gh PR lookup fails or returns malformed JSON; subsequent fallback calls succeed. The factory pushes the old verified SHA and opens a draft without reporting the HEAD mismatch, violating the requested no-push b

review-127.title: Pending-merge exception accepts unreviewed amendments
review-127.detail: validateMerge checks only the two parent SHAs, so amending a pending factory merge with arbitrary file changes still satisfies this exception. On resume, mergeForDelivery accepts that amended merge, runs post-merge gates, and records it as the delivery head without auditing or reviewing the amendment. The requested refusal therefore remains bypassable. An isolated probe executing the actual helper and validator against real git failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/delivery-head-probe.ts"` printed `refused: false` and `AssertionError: An amended pending merge must be refused before delivery`.
review-127.failure_scenario: Interrupt delivery during post-merge gates while pendingRebaseSha and preRebaseHead remain persisted. Amend the merge commit to change application code, preserving both parents, then resume with passing gates. The helper accepts and delivery pushes the unreviewed amendment instead of ending needs_hu

review-127.title: Do not authorize a changed merge commit from its parents alone
review-127.detail: When pendingRebaseSha is set, this exception accepts any HEAD with the expected two parents. validateMerge checks ancestry, not the commit's tree or an exact recorded SHA. Amending a pending clean merge preserves those parents, so resume accepts the unreviewed amendment, reruns post-merge gates, and pushes it without review or audit. A temporary Git fixture invoking validateMerge after such an amendment printed: `validateMerge accepted amended, unreviewed HEAD: ce8e0282e9e7af6360d1efdead30a1c22a0656d6`.
review-127.failure_scenario: Interrupt new-PR delivery during post-merge gates while pendingRebaseSha is persisted. Amend the merge commit to change a file without changing its parents, then resume. If the gates pass, the amended commit is pushed instead of ending needs_human.

review-060.title: Cleanup failures from the finally block still fail the run
review-060.detail: The handler recognizes only WorktreeCleanError from the initial checkoutCommitted call. The unconditional discardChanges in the gates' finally block uses git clean -fdq without retry and throws an ordinary CommandError. That bypasses this handler even after a stuck implementer. Its exception can also replace an initial WorktreeCleanError, defeating the new recovery path.
review-060.failure_scenario: A stuck implementer's partial changes reach gates. Gates leave an untracked output directory and the final git clean -fdq fails once. The run fails immediately instead of retrying cleanup or proceeding to another implementation round.

review-129.title: Compact output still includes an unbounded dependency array
review-129.detail: compactRun copies every dependsOn entry. Dependency counts have no input limit, so clipping title and error does not bound default output size. A read-only `bun run -` probe executing the extracted compactRun with 1,200 dependencies and short scalar fields printed `compact get_run size with 1200 dependencies: 30186`, exceeding both newly tested byte budgets before MCP envelope overhead.
review-129.failure_scenario: Inspect a run depending on 1,200 existing runs, or list several runs with large dependency arrays; default tool output again exceeds the intended compact byte budget.

review-129.title: Repository filtering silently fails against the previous daemon
review-129.detail: The proxy relies entirely on the new HTTP repo parameter. The base daemon ignores that parameter and limits across all repositories, so a newer MCP client returns unrelated runs and incorrect hasMore information. A focused check using the actual httpBackend with a base-compatible response failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-review.ts" skew` printed `requested target/repo; received: [{"id":"other","repoSlug":"other/repo"}]`, followed by `AssertionError: false == true`.
review-129.failure_scenario: A newer stdio MCP client connects to the previous running daemon and calls limitless_list_runs with repo set to target/repo while newer runs belong to other/repo.

review-129.title: Compact output retains an unbounded dependency array
review-129.detail: Both default inspection tools copy every dependency ID into their compact output. Dependency validation imposes no count limit, so valid fan-in runs still exceed the intended byte budgets. A focused check executing the actual compactRun function failed: `bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-review.ts" size` printed `compactRun bytes: 33185; expected < 4096`, followed by `AssertionError: false == true`. Five such runs also exceed the list test's 16 KB budget.
review-129.failure_scenario: A valid run depends on 1,000 existing runs. Default get_run returns over 33 KB before adding state and land information; a default list containing several such runs is substantially larger.

review-129.title: Compact responses still include an unbounded dependency array
review-129.detail: compactRun copies every dependency ID. Dependency validation imposes no count limit, so one valid run can exceed the response budget regardless of the default five-run limit or title/error clipping. An isolated probe exercised the extracted compactRun with 2,000 distinct dependency IDs. Command: TMP="$TMPDIR" TEMP="$TMPDIR" bun "$TMPDIR/mcp-review-check.ts" size. Output: "default list response with one run depending on 2000 runs: 34299 bytes" and "AssertionError: default list exceeds the new 16 KiB regression budget". Larger dependency lists can recreate the original oversized-output failure in both list and get.
review-129.failure_scenario: A run aggregates thousands of existing runs through dependsOn and appears in the default list or is inspected with the default get_run option.

review-129.title: Repository filtering silently fails against the previous daemon
review-129.detail: The proxy delegates filtering entirely to the new HTTP repo parameter. The base daemon ignores that parameter, so a newer CLI connected to the previous release returns unrelated repositories. The tool then limits those results and computes hasMore as though filtering succeeded. Reproduction command: `bun /private/tmp/lr-7UZxPn/claude-501/mcp-version-skew.ts`. This executes the changed httpBackend against an injected fetcher implementing the base endpoint's behavior. Output: `{"requestedRepo":"target/repo","actual":[{"id":"new-other","repoSlug":"other/repo"},{"id":"old-target","repoSlug":"target/repo"}]}`, followed by `AssertionError: Repository-filtered list returned another repository again
review-129.failure_scenario: A new MCP CLI connects to the previous daemon. Another repository has the newest run. Calling limitless_list_runs with repo='target/repo' and limit=1 returns the other repository's run and excludes the matching older run.
